title.zh: 卷二十二 列傳第十二 王曇首
title.raw: 卷二十二 列傳第十二 王曇首 Volume 22 Biographies 12: Wang Tanshou

sentences.zh: 列傳第十二

translations.literal: Biographies 12
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 12

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，車駕出北堂，使三更竟，開廣莫門。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia, the imperial carriage went out through the North Hall; at the end of the third watch the Guangmo Gate was to be opened.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 4 the emperor left by the North Hall and ordered the Guangmo Gate opened at the end of the third watch.

sentences.zh: 南台雲，「應須白獸幡、銀字檀」。

translations.literal: The Southern Office said, "White-beast banners and silver-lettered sandalwood are required."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Office reported that white-beast banners and silver-lettered sandalwood were required.

sentences.zh: 不肯開。

translations.literal: They refused to open it.
translations.idiomatic: They refused to open it.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞羊玄保奏免御史中丞傅隆以下。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Xuanbao memorialized to dismiss the Censor-in-Chief Fu Long and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Xuanbao memorialized for the dismissal of Censor-in-Chief Fu Long and his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 曇首曰：「既無墨敕，又闕幡檀，雖稱上旨，不異單刺。

translations.literal: Tanshou said, "With no ink edict and no banners or sandalwood, though it is called the sovereign's intent, it is no different from a lone dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou said, "Without an ink edict and without the banners and sandalwood, though it is called the emperor's wish, it is no different from a private order.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年、二年，雖有再開門例，此乃前事之違。

translations.literal: In the first and second years of Yuanjia there were precedents of opening the gate twice; those were violations of earlier practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 1 and 2 did see the gate opened twice, but those were departures from earlier precedent.

sentences.zh: 今之守舊，未為非禮。

translations.literal: To hold to the old rule now is not contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Upholding the established rule now is not improper.

sentences.zh: 其不請白獸幡、銀字檀，致開門不時，由尚書相承之失，亦合糾正。

translations.literal: That white-beast banners and silver-lettered sandalwood were not requested, causing the gate not to open on time, was a failure handed down through the Masters of Writing and should also be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The failure to request the white-beast banners and silver-lettered sandalwood, which made the gate open late, was a lapse inherited from the Masters of Writing and ought to be corrected as well.

sentences.zh: 」上特無問，更立科條。

translations.literal: " The emperor specially made no inquiry and instead established new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took no action against them and instead issued new regulations.

sentences.zh: 遷太子詹事，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent while remaining Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 自謝晦平後，上欲封曇首等，會燕集，舉酒勸之，因拊御床曰：「此坐非卿兄弟，無復今日。

translations.literal: After Xie Hui was pacified, the emperor wished to ennoble Tanshou and others; at a banquet he raised his cup to urge them and, patting the imperial couch, said, "This seat would not be yours, brothers, were it not for today.
translations.idiomatic: After Xie Hui's rebellion was crushed, the emperor wished to ennoble Tanshou and his colleagues; at a feast he raised his cup to them and, striking the imperial couch, said, "But for you, brothers, I would not be sitting here today.

sentences.zh: 」出詔以示之。

translations.literal: He produced the edict to show them.
translations.idiomatic: He produced the edict for them to see.

sentences.zh: 曇首曰：「豈可因國之災，以為身幸。

translations.literal: Tanshou said, "How can one turn the realm's disaster into personal fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou said, "How can one treat the realm's calamity as private gain?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲私臣，當如直史何。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty wishes to favor your minister, what of the upright historians?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty wishes to favor me, what will the upright historians say?

sentences.zh: 」封事遂寢。

translations.literal: The enfeoffment was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時弘錄尚書事，又為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Hong was Recorder of the Masters of Writing and also Governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Hong served as Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 曇首為上所親委，任兼兩宮。

translations.literal: Tanshou was personally entrusted by the emperor and held duties in both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou enjoyed the emperor's personal trust and held responsibilities in both palaces.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康與弘並錄，意常怏怏，又欲得揚州。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and Hong were both Recorders, and Yikang was often discontent; he also wanted Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang and Hong both served as Recorders; Yikang was often resentful and also coveted Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 以曇首居中分其權任，愈不悅。

translations.literal: Because Tanshou stood at the center and divided his power and duties, he grew even less pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tanshou occupied the center and split his authority, Yikang grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 曇首固乞吳郡，文帝曰：「豈有欲建大廈而遺其棟樑？

translations.literal: Tanshou firmly begged for Wu commandery; Emperor Wen said, "When one wishes to raise a great hall, can one discard its beams and pillars?
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou repeatedly asked to be sent to Wu commandery. Emperor Wen said, "When you mean to raise a great hall, would you cast away its beams and pillars?

sentences.zh: 賢兄比屢稱疾，固辭州任，將來若相申許，此處非卿而誰？

translations.literal: Your worthy elder brother has repeatedly pleaded illness and firmly declined provincial office; if in future I should grant his request, who but you should hold this post?
translations.idiomatic: Your worthy brother has often pleaded illness and refused provincial appointment; if I should grant his wish in time, who but you should fill this post?

sentences.zh: 」時弘久疾，屢遜位，不許。

translations.literal: At the time Hong had long been ill and repeatedly yielded his rank, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had been ill for some time and repeatedly tried to resign, but was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 義康謂賓客曰：「王公久疾不起，神州詎合臥臨？

translations.literal: Yikang said to his guests, "Lord Wang has long been ill and cannot rise; should the heartland lie under a sickbed?
translations.idiomatic: Yikang told his guests, "Lord Wang has lain ill so long he cannot rise—should the heartland be governed from a sickbed?

sentences.zh: 」曇首勸弘減府兵力之半，以配義康，乃悅。

translations.literal: Tanshou urged Hong to cut the prefectural military strength by half and assign it to Yikang, and Yikang was then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshou persuaded Hong to halve the prefectural military force and assign half to Yikang, and Yikang was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，時年三十七。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year, at thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 文帝臨慟，歎曰：「王詹事所疾不救，國之衰也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen came in person to mourn and sighed, "The illness of Grand Mentor Wang could not be cured—this is the realm's decline.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen mourned in person and sighed, "Grand Mentor Wang's illness could not be cured—the realm itself is failing.

sentences.zh: 」中書舍人周赳侍側曰：「王家欲衰，賢者先殞。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Zhou Jiu, attending at his side, said, "When the Wang house is about to decline, the worthy die first.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Zhou Jiu, standing beside him, said, "When a great house is about to fall, the worthy perish first.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「直是我家衰耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "It is simply my own house that is declining.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "It is simply my own house that is declining.

sentences.zh: 」贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 九年，以預誅徐羨之等謀，追封豫甯縣侯，諡曰文。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for his part in the plot to execute Xu Xianzhi and others, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yunin with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, for his role in the plot against Xu Xianzhi and others, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yunin with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，配饗文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu acceded, Tanshou was given a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Wen's temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Tanshou was given a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Wen's temple.

sentences.zh: 子僧綽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Sengchuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengchuo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 僧綽幼有大成之度，眾便以國器許之。

translations.literal: From childhood Sengchuo had the measure of great accomplishment; the multitude already regarded him as material for state service.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Sengchuo showed the makings of greatness; people already hailed him as destined for high office.

sentences.zh: 好學，練悉朝典。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was thoroughly versed in court regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He loved study and knew court regulations inside out.

sentences.zh: 年十三，文帝引見，拜便流涕哽咽，上亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: At thirteen Emperor Wen summoned him; upon bowing he wept and choked, and the emperor too was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Emperor Wen received him in audience; when he bowed he wept and choked, and the emperor too was overcome.

sentences.zh: 襲封豫甯縣侯，尚文帝長女東陽獻公主。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate of Yunin and married Emperor Wen's eldest daughter, Princess Xian of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he inherited the marquisate of Yunin and married Emperor Wen's eldest daughter, Princess Xian of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 初為江夏王義恭司徒參軍。

translations.literal: At first he served as aide to Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as aide to Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, in his capacity as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書吏部郎，參掌大選，究識流品，任舉咸盡其分。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to Director of the Personnel Section of the Masters of Writing, sharing charge of major selections; he thoroughly knew ranks and types, and every appointment matched its proper level.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Personnel Section and shared charge of major appointments; he knew every rank and type, and each posting matched its proper level.

sentences.zh: 僧綽深沈有局度，不以才能高人。

translations.literal: Sengchuo was deep and steady with breadth of view, and did not set himself above others by talent.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo was deep and steady in bearing and never lorded his talent over others.

sentences.zh: 父曇首與王華並被任遇，華子新建侯嗣，才劣位遇亦輕。

translations.literal: His father Tanshou and Wang Hua were both favored with appointment; Hua's son the Marquis of Xinjian, Si, was inferior in talent and lightly regarded in rank.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanshou and Wang Hua both enjoyed imperial favor; Hua's son Si, Marquis of Xinjian, was lesser in talent and lightly regarded in office.

sentences.zh: 僧綽嘗謂中書侍郎蔡興宗曰：「弟名位應與新建齊，弟超至今日，蓋姻戚所致也。

translations.literal: Sengchuo once said to Palace Secretary Cai Xingzong, "My name and rank ought to match Xinjian's; that I have risen to today is surely due to marriage ties.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo once told Palace Secretary Cai Xingzong, "My name and rank ought to match the Marquis of Xinjian's; that I have risen so far is surely due to marriage connections.

sentences.zh: 」遷侍中，時年二十九。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant at the age of twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant at twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚嘗問其年，僧綽自嫌早達，逡巡良久乃答，其謙退若此。

translations.literal: Prince of Shixing Jun once asked his age; Sengchuo, ashamed of early advancement, hesitated a long while before answering—such was his modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shixing Jun once asked his age; ashamed of his early rise, Sengchuo hesitated long before answering—such was his modesty.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，文帝頗以後事為念，大相付託，朝政大小皆參焉。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia Emperor Wen greatly concerned himself with affairs after his death and entrusted much to Sengchuo; he took part in all matters great and small in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanjia Emperor Wen brooded over the succession and entrusted much to Sengchuo, who took part in every major and minor matter of state.

sentences.zh: 從兄微，清介士也，懼其太盛，勸令損抑。

translations.literal: His cousin Wei was a man of pure integrity and, fearing Sengchuo's power had grown too great, urged him to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Wei was a man of pure integrity; fearing Sengchuo's power had grown too great, he urged restraint.

sentences.zh: 僧綽乃求吳郡及廣州，並不許。

translations.literal: Sengchuo then requested Wu commandery and Guang Province, and was denied both.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo then asked for Wu commandery and Guang Province; both requests were denied.

sentences.zh: 會巫蠱事泄，上先召僧綽具言之。

translations.literal: When the witchcraft affair leaked out, the emperor first summoned Sengchuo and told him everything.
translations.idiomatic: When the witchcraft affair came to light, the emperor first summoned Sengchuo and told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 及將廢立，使尋求前朝舊典。

translations.literal: When the heir was to be deposed and another installed, he was sent to seek precedents from former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir was to be deposed and another raised, he was sent to gather precedents from earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 劭於東宮夜饗將士，僧綽密以啟聞。

translations.literal: Shao feasted his officers in the Eastern Palace by night; Sengchuo secretly reported this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shao feasted his officers in the Eastern Palace by night; Sengchuo secretly reported it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上又令撰漢、魏以來廢諸王故事送與江湛、徐湛之。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered him to compile stories of deposed princes from Han and Wei onward and send them to Jiang Zhan and Xu Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered him to compile accounts of deposed princes from Han and Wei onward and send them to Jiang Zhan and Xu Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 湛之欲立隨王誕，江湛欲立南平王鑠，文帝欲立建平王宏，議久不決。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi wished to install Prince of Suixing Dan; Jiang Zhan wished Prince of Nanping Shuo; Emperor Wen wished Prince of Jianping Hong; deliberation long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi favored Prince of Suixing Dan; Jiang Zhan favored Prince of Nanping Shuo; Emperor Wen favored Prince of Jianping Hong; deliberation dragged on without decision.

sentences.zh: 誕妃即湛之女，鑠妃湛妹也。

translations.literal: Dan's consort was Xu Xianzhi's daughter; Shuo's consort was Jiang Zhan's sister.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's consort was Xu Xianzhi's daughter—Shuo's consort was Jiang Zhan's sister.

sentences.zh: 僧綽曰：「建立之事，仰由聖懷。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "The matter of establishing an heir rests on the sacred mind.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said, "The choice of heir rests with Your Majesty's sacred judgment.

sentences.zh: 臣謂惟宜速斷，幾事雖密，不可使難生慮表，取笑千載。

translations.literal: Your minister holds that a swift decision is best; though the affair is secret, one must not let difficulty breed outward concern and become a jest for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I believe you should decide quickly; though the matter is secret, delay breeds rumor and will make us a laughingstock for ages.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿可謂能斷大事，此事不可不殷勤；

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You may be called able to decide great affairs; this matter cannot but be handled with care;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You may be called able to decide great affairs; this cannot be handled carelessly;

sentences.zh: 且庶人始亡，人將謂我無復慈愛之道。

translations.literal: moreover the commoner has just died—people will say I no longer know fatherly love.
translations.idiomatic: moreover the heir has just been condemned—people will say I no longer know fatherly love.

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「恐千載之後，言陛下惟能裁弟，不能裁兒。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "I fear that after a thousand years men will say Your Majesty could cut down a younger brother but not a son.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said, "I fear that ages hence men will say Your Majesty could cut down a brother but not a son.

sentences.zh: 」上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 江湛出合謂僧綽曰：「卿向言將不傷直邪？

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan came out of the privy chamber and said to Sengchuo, "Will what you just said not harm your integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan came out of the privy chamber and told Sengchuo, "Will what you just said not harm your integrity?

sentences.zh: 」僧綽曰：「弟亦恨君不直。」

translations.literal: Sengchuo said, "I too regret that you are not upright."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo replied, "I too regret that you are not upright."

sentences.zh: 及劭弑逆，江湛在尚書上省，聞變，曰：「不用王僧綽言至此。

translations.literal: When Shao committed regicide, Jiang Zhan was in the upper office of the Masters of Writing; hearing of the upheaval he said, "Had Wang Sengchuo's words been heeded, it would not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao murdered his father, Jiang Zhan was in the upper office of the Masters of Writing; hearing of the upheaval he said, "Had Wang Sengchuo's counsel been heeded, it would not have come to this.

sentences.zh: 」劭立，轉僧綽吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Shao took the throne, Sengchuo was transferred to Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao took the throne, Sengchuo was made Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及檢文帝巾箱及湛家書疏，得僧綽所啟饗士並廢諸王事，乃收害焉，因此陷北第諸侯王，以為與僧綽有異志。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen's document box and Jiang Zhan's household letters were searched, Sengchuo's reports on the feast of officers and the deposed princes were found; he was seized and killed, and on this pretext the princes of the Northern Residence were implicated as sharing Sengchuo's disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen's document box and Jiang Zhan's household correspondence were searched, Sengchuo's reports on the officers' feast and the deposed princes were found; he was seized and executed, and on this pretext the princes of the Northern Residence were implicated as sharing his disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，追贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰湣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu acceded, Sengchuo was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with the posthumous title Marquis Min.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Sengchuo was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with the posthumous title Marquis Min.

sentences.zh: 初，太社西空地，本吳時丁奉宅，孫皓流徙其家。

translations.literal: At first the empty ground west of the Great Altar of Soil and Grain had been Ding Feng's residence in Wu times; Sun Hao exiled his household.
translations.idiomatic: At first the empty ground west of the Great Altar of Soil and Grain had been Ding Feng's residence in Wu times; Sun Hao exiled his household from it.

sentences.zh: 江左初，為周顗、蘇峻宅，後為袁悅宅，又為章武王司馬秀宅，皆以凶終；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Eastern Jin it became the residence of Zhou Yi and Su Jun, later of Yuan Yue, then of Sima Xiu, Marshal of Prince of Zhangwu; all met violent ends;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Eastern Jin it became the residence of Zhou Yi and Su Jun, later of Yuan Yue, then of Sima Xiu, Marshal of Prince of Zhangwu—all met violent ends;

sentences.zh: 及給臧燾，亦頻遇禍，故世稱凶地。

translations.literal: when it was given to Zang Tao, he too repeatedly met disaster, so the world called it an ill-omened place.
translations.idiomatic: when it was given to Zang Tao—he too repeatedly met disaster, so the world called it an ill-omened place.

sentences.zh: 僧綽嘗謂宅無吉凶，請以為第，始造，未及居而敗。

translations.literal: Sengchuo once said dwellings had no lucky or unlucky and asked to make it his residence; he had just begun building when, before he could move in, he was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo once said dwellings had no lucky or unlucky and asked to build his residence there; construction had barely begun when, before he could move in, he was ruined.

sentences.zh: 子儉。

translations.literal: His son Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jian.

sentences.zh: 儉字仲寶，生而僧綽遇害，為叔父僧虔所養。

translations.literal: Jian, styled Zhongbao, was born as Sengchuo was killed and was raised by his uncle Sengqian.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, courtesy name Zhongbao, was born as Sengchuo was killed and was raised by his uncle Sengqian.

sentences.zh: 數歲，襲爵豫甯縣侯。

translations.literal: At several years of age he inherited the marquisate of Yunin.
translations.idiomatic: At a few years of age he inherited the marquisate of Yunin.

sentences.zh: 拜受茅土，流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: Receiving the fief soil, he wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the fief soil he wept and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 幼篤學，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: From youth he was devoted to learning and never put down his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was devoted to learning and never put down his scrolls.

sentences.zh: 賓客或相稱美，僧虔曰：「我不患此兒無名，政恐名太盛耳。

translations.literal: When guests praised him, Sengqian said, "I do not fear this boy lacking fame; I only fear his fame will grow too great.
translations.idiomatic: When guests praised him, Sengqian said, "I do not fear this boy will lack renown; I only fear his renown will grow too great.

sentences.zh: 」乃手書崔子玉座右銘以貽之。

translations.literal: He personally wrote out Cui Yuan's Inscription at the Seat and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: He personally copied Cui Yuan's Inscription at the Seat and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹袁粲聞其名，及見之曰：「宰相之門也。

translations.literal: Governor of Danyang Yuan Can heard his name and, upon meeting him, said, "This is the gate of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Danyang Yuan Can heard his name and, upon meeting him, said, "This is the household of a future chief minister.

sentences.zh: 栝柏豫章雖小，已有棟樑氣矣，終當任人家國事。

translations.literal: Though cypress and zhang wood of Yuzhang are small, they already have the air of beams and pillars; in the end he will bear the affairs of others' houses and states.
translations.idiomatic: Though cypress and zhang wood of Yuzhang are small, they already have the air of beams and pillars; in time he will bear the weight of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」言之宋明帝，選尚陽羨公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He spoke of this to Emperor Ming of Song, who chose him to marry Princess Yangxian and made him Commandant of the Horse Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of this to Emperor Ming of Song, who chose Jian to marry Princess Yangxian and made him Commandant of the Horse Guard.

sentences.zh: 帝以儉嫡母武康公主同太初巫蠱事，不可以為婦姑，欲開塚離葬。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Jian's principal mother Princess Wukang was implicated in the Taichu witchcraft affair and could not be mother-in-law to the princess, wished to open the tomb and rebury her separately.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jian's principal mother Princess Wukang had been implicated in the Taichu witchcraft affair and could not stand as mother-in-law to the princess, the emperor wished to open the tomb and rebury her separately.

sentences.zh: 儉因人自陳，密以死請，故事不行。

translations.literal: Jian pleaded through an intermediary and secretly begged with his life; the precedent was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Jian pleaded through an intermediary and secretly begged with his life; the plan was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 年十八，解褐秘書郎，太子舍人，超遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: At eighteen he left office as Secretary and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and was promoted over the usual course to Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he left office as Secretary and Attendant of the Heir Apparent and was promoted over the usual course to Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 依七略撰七志四十卷，表獻之。

translations.literal: Following the Seven Summaries he compiled the Seven Records in forty scrolls and presented them in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Seven Summaries he compiled the Seven Records in forty scrolls and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又撰定元徽四部書目。

translations.literal: He also compiled and fixed the Yuanhui four-division book catalogue.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he also compiled and fixed the Yuanhui four-division book catalogue.

sentences.zh: 母憂，服闋，為司徒右長史。

translations.literal: After his mother's mourning and the end of mourning, he became Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother and completing the rites, he became Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 晉令，公府長史著朝服，宋大明以來著朱衣。

translations.literal: Jin regulations required the chief secretary of a duke's office to wear court robes; from the Da Ming era of Song onward they wore vermilion garments.
translations.idiomatic: Jin regulations required the chief secretary of a duke's office to wear court robes; from Song's Da Ming era onward they wore vermilion garments.

sentences.zh: 儉上言宜復舊制，時議不許。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized that the old system should be restored; at the time the deliberation did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian memorialized that the old system should be restored; the court did not approve.

sentences.zh: 及蒼梧暴虐，儉告袁粲求外出，引晉新安主婿王獻之任吳興為例，補義興太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cangwu was violent and cruel, Jian told Yuan Can he sought an outside post, citing as precedent Wang Xianzhi, son-in-law of the Prince of Xin'an, who had served as Governor of Wuxing, and was appointed Governor of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cangwu turned violent and cruel, Jian told Yuan Can he wished to leave the capital, citing as precedent Wang Xianzhi, son-in-law of the Prince of Xin'an, who had served as Governor of Wuxing; he was appointed Governor of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 升明二年，為長兼侍中，以父終此職，固讓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he served concurrently as Senior Palace Attendant; because his father had ended his life in this office, he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 he served concurrently as Senior Palace Attendant; because his father had died in that office, he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊高帝為相，欲引時賢參贊大業，時謝朏為長史，帝夜召朏，卻人與語久之，朏無言。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Gao of Qi as regent wished to bring in men of the age to assist the great enterprise; at the time Xie Tiao was chief secretary; the emperor summoned Tiao at night, dismissed attendants, and spoke with him at length, but Tiao said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Gao of Qi was regent he wished to bring in leading men to assist the great enterprise; Xie Tiao was chief secretary at the time; the emperor summoned Tiao at night, dismissed attendants, and spoke with him at length, but Tiao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 唯有二小兒捉燭，帝慮朏難之，仍取燭遣兒，朏又無言，帝乃呼左右。

translations.literal: Only two small boys held candles; the emperor, fearing Tiao found it difficult, then took the candles and sent the boys away, but Tiao again said nothing, and the emperor then called attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Only two small boys held candles; fearing Tiao found the situation awkward, the emperor took the candles and sent the boys away, but Tiao still said nothing, and the emperor finally called attendants.

sentences.zh: 儉素知帝雄異，後請間言於帝曰：「功高不賞，古來非一，以公今日位地，欲北面居人臣，可乎？

translations.literal: Jian had long known the emperor's heroic difference; afterward he asked privately and said to the emperor, "Merit too high to reward—since antiquity this has not been rare; in your present rank and position, can you face north and remain another's minister?
translations.idiomatic: Jian had long sensed the emperor's extraordinary ambition; afterward he asked for a private word and said, "Merit too high to reward is not rare in history; in your present rank and position, can you face north and remain another man's minister?

sentences.zh: 」帝正色裁之，而神采內和。

translations.literal: The emperor sternly checked him, yet inwardly his spirit was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sternly rebuked him, yet inwardly his spirit was at ease.

sentences.zh: 儉因又曰：「儉蒙公殊眄，所以吐所難吐，何賜拒之深。

translations.literal: Jian then said again, "Jian has received your special regard, and therefore speaks what is hard to speak—why grant refusal so deep?
translations.idiomatic: Jian then said again, "I have received your special regard, and therefore speak what is hard to speak—why reject me so harshly?

sentences.zh: 宋以景和、元徽之淫虐，非公豈復寧濟；

translations.literal: Song, because of Jinghe and Yuanhui's debauchery and cruelty, would not have been restored to peace but for you;
translations.idiomatic: Song—because of Jinghe and Yuanhui's debauchery and cruelty, would not have been restored to peace but for you;

sentences.zh: 但人情澆薄，不能持久，公若小復推遷，則人望去矣，豈唯大業永淪，七尺豈可得保？

translations.literal: but human hearts are thin and cannot long endure; if you again defer and yield a little, men will turn away—not only will the great enterprise sink forever, but how can even your own person be preserved?
translations.idiomatic: but human hearts are fickle and cannot long endure; if you defer and yield again, men will turn away—not only will the great enterprise be lost forever, but how can even your own person be preserved?

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿言不無理。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said, "Your words are not without reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and replied, "Your words are not without reason.

sentences.zh: 」儉又曰：「公今名位，故是經常宰相，宜禮絕群後，微示變革。

translations.literal: Jian also said, "Your present name and rank are still those of an ordinary chief minister; you should stand above the host of officials in ritual and show change in small ways.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also said, "Your present name and rank are still those of an ordinary chief minister; you should stand above the host of officials in ritual and signal change in small ways.

sentences.zh: 當先令褚公知之，儉請銜命。

translations.literal: First let Lord Chu know; Jian asks to carry the command.
translations.idiomatic: First let Lord Chu know; I ask to carry the command.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我當自往。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I shall go myself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I shall go myself.

sentences.zh: 」經少日，帝自造彥回，款言移晷，乃謂曰：「我夢應得官。

translations.literal: " After several days the emperor went in person to Yanhui and spoke at length in earnest tones, then said, "My dream says I should receive office.
translations.idiomatic: " After several days the emperor went in person to Yanhui and spoke at length in earnest tones, then replied, "My dream says I should receive office.

sentences.zh: 」彥回曰：「今授始爾，恐一二年間未容便移。

translations.literal: Yanhui said, "You have just received appointment; I fear that within a year or two it cannot yet be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui replied, "You have just received appointment; I fear that within a year or two it cannot yet be moved.

sentences.zh: 且吉夢未必便在旦夕。

translations.literal: Moreover an auspicious dream is not necessarily fulfilled at once.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: moreover an auspicious dream is not necessarily fulfilled at once.

sentences.zh: 」帝還告儉，儉曰：「褚是未達理。

translations.literal: The emperor returned and told Jian; Jian said, "Chu does not yet grasp the principle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned and told Jian; Jian replied, "Chu does not yet grasp the principle.

sentences.zh: 」虞整時為中書舍人，甚閑辭翰，儉乃自報整，使作詔。

translations.literal: Yu Zheng was then Palace Secretary and very skilled in drafting; Jian reported to Zheng himself and had him compose the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zheng was then Palace Secretary and very skilled in drafting—Jian reported to Zheng himself and had him compose the edict.

sentences.zh: 及高帝為太尉，引儉為右長史，尋轉左，專見任用。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor became Grand Commandant he appointed Jian Senior Secretary, then transferred him to the left and gave him sole trust.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: when the High Emperor became Grand Commandant he appointed Jian Senior Secretary, then transferred him to the left and gave him sole trust.

sentences.zh: 大典將行，禮儀詔策，皆出於儉，褚彥回唯為禪詔，又使儉參懷定之。

translations.literal: When the great ceremony was about to be performed, ritual, edicts, and proclamations all came from Jian; Chu Yanhui alone drafted the abdication edict, and Jian was also made to consult and fix it.
translations.idiomatic: When the great ceremony was about to be performed, ritual, edicts, and proclamations all came from Jian—Chu Yanhui alone drafted the abdication edict, and Jian was also made to consult and fix it.

sentences.zh: 齊台建，遷尚書右僕射，領吏部，時年二十八。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, Jian was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of Personnel, aged twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established, Jian was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Director of Personnel at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 多所引進。

translations.literal: He brought in many men.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he brought in many men.

sentences.zh: 時客有姓譚者，詣儉求官，儉謂曰：「齊桓滅譚，那得有君？

translations.literal: At the time a client surnamed Tan came to Jian seeking office; Jian said to him, "When Duke Huan of Qi destroyed Tan, how could there still be a lord?
translations.idiomatic: At the time a client surnamed Tan came to Jian seeking office; Jian told him, "When Duke Huan of Qi destroyed Tan, how could there still be a lord?

sentences.zh: 「答曰：「譚子奔莒，所以有僕。

translations.literal: He answered, "Tanzi fled to Ju—therefore there is a servant.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Tanzi fled to Ju—therefore I am here.

sentences.zh: 」儉賞其善據，卒得職焉。

translations.literal: Jian admired his good citation and in the end he obtained a post.
translations.idiomatic: Jian admired his clever citation and in the end he obtained a post.

sentences.zh: 高帝嘗從容謂儉曰：「我今日當以青溪為鴻溝。

translations.literal: The High Emperor once said at ease to Jian, "Today I shall take the Qing Stream as the Hong Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor once said at ease to Jian—"Today I shall take the Qing Stream as the Hong Canal.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「天應人順，庶無楚、漢之事。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Heaven responds and men follow—there will likely be no Chu-Han affair."
translations.idiomatic: He replied—"Heaven responds and men follow—there will likely be no Chu-Han affair."

sentences.zh: 時朝儀草創，衣服制則，未有定準，儉議曰：「漢景六年，梁王入朝，中郎謁者金貂出入殿門。

translations.literal: At the time court ritual was newly established and dress regulations had no fixed standard; Jian argued, "In the sixth year of Han Jingdi, the King of Liang entered court and the palace attendant with the golden sable entered and left the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time court ritual was newly established and dress regulations had no fixed standard; Jian argued, "In Han Jingdi 6 the King of Liang entered court and the palace attendant with the golden sable entered and left the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 左思魏都賦雲'藹藹列侍，金貂齊光'，此藩國侍臣有貂之明文。

translations.literal: Left Si's Rhapsody on the Capital of Wei says 'thickly ranked attendants, golden sables gleaming together'—this is clear text that feudal attendants had sables.
translations.idiomatic: Left Si's Rhapsody on the Capital of Wei says 'thickly ranked attendants, golden sables gleaming together'—this is clear text that feudal attendants wore sables.

sentences.zh: 晉百官表雲'太尉參軍四人，朝服武冠'，此又宰府之明文。

translations.literal: The Jin table of officials says 'Grand Commandant has four aides, court robes and martial cap'—this is again clear text of the chief minister's office.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: the Jin table of officials says 'Grand Commandant has four aides, court robes and martial cap'—this is again clear text of the chief minister's office.

sentences.zh: 」又疑百僚敬齊公之禮，儉又曰：「晉王受命，勸進雲，'沖等眷眷'，稱名則應盡禮。

translations.literal: He also doubted the ritual of the hundred officials' reverence toward the Duke of Qi; Jian also said, "When the Prince of Jin received the mandate, the address of urging accession says 'Chong and others look earnestly'—when naming names, full ritual should apply.
translations.idiomatic: He also questioned the ritual of the hundred officials' reverence toward the Duke of Qi; Jian also said, "When the Prince of Jin received the mandate, the address of urging accession says 'Chong and others look earnestly'—when naming names, full ritual should apply.

sentences.zh: 」而世子禮秩未定，儉又曰：「春秋曹世子來朝，待以上公之禮，下其君一等。

translations.literal: The heir's ritual rank was undetermined; Jian also said, "In Spring and Autumn when the heir of Cao came to court, he was treated with the ritual of upper duke, one rank below his lord.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's ritual rank was undetermined; Jian also replied, "In Spring and Autumn when the heir of Cao came to court, he was treated with the ritual of upper duke, one rank below his lord.

sentences.zh: 今齊公九命，禮冠列蕃，世子亦宜異數。

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Qi has nine appointments and ritual crowns the feudal lords; the heir too should have a distinct number.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Duke of Qi has nine appointments and ritual crowns the feudal lords; the heir too should have a distinct rank.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All were followed.

sentences.zh: 世子鎮石頭城，仍以為世子宮，儉又曰：「魯有靈光殿，漢之前例也。

translations.literal: The heir garrisoned Stone City and it was also made the heir's palace; Jian also said, "Lu had the Luminous Hall—this is a Han precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The heir garrisoned Stone City and it was also made the heir's palace; Jian also replied, "Lu had the Luminous Hall—this is a Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 聽事為崇光殿，外齋為宣德殿，以散騎常侍張緒為世子詹事，車服悉依東宮制度。」

translations.literal: The reception hall was the Hall of Honored Light, the outer study the Hall of Proclaimed Virtue; Attendant Cavalier Regular Zhang Xu was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, carriage and dress all following Eastern Palace regulations."
translations.idiomatic: The reception hall was the Hall of Honored Light, the outer study the Hall of Proclaimed Virtue—Attendant Cavalier Regular Zhang Xu was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, carriage and dress all following Eastern Palace regulations."

sentences.zh: 高帝踐阼，與儉議佐命功臣，從容謂曰：「卿謀謨之功，莫與為二，卿止二千戶，意以為少。

translations.literal: When the High Emperor ascended the throne he discussed with Jian the merit-bearing ministers who aided the mandate and said at ease, "Your counsel and planning have no second; you have only two thousand households—I think it too few.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Emperor ascended the throne he discussed with Jian the merit-bearing ministers who aided the mandate and said at ease, "Your counsel and planning have no second—you have only two thousand households—I think it too few.

sentences.zh: 趙充國猶能自舉西零之任，況卿與我情期異常。

translations.literal: Zhao Chongguo could still recommend himself for the Western Zero mission—how much more you, with whom my bond is extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: zhao Chongguo could still recommend himself for the Western Zero mission—how much more you, with whom my bond is extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「昔宋祖創業，佐命諸公，開國不過二千，以臣比之，唯覺超越。

translations.literal: Jian said, "When Emperor Wu of Song founded the enterprise, the merit-bearing ministers who aided the mandate received no more than two thousand households in enfeoffment; compared with them, I only feel I have exceeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "When Emperor Wu of Song founded the enterprise, the merit-bearing ministers who aided the mandate received no more than two thousand households in enfeoffment; compared with them, I only feel I have exceeded.

sentences.zh: 」上笑曰：「張良辭侯，何以過此。」

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said, "When Zhang Liang declined a marquisate, how could he surpass this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and replied, "When Zhang Liang declined a marquisate, how could he surpass this."

sentences.zh: 建元元年，改封南昌縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 1 he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 時都下舛雜，且多奸盜，上欲立符伍，家家以相檢括。

translations.literal: At the time the capital was disorderly and there were many thieves and rogues; the emperor wished to establish tally-neighborhoods so every household would inspect one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the capital was disorderly and there were many thieves and rogues; the emperor wished to establish tally-neighborhoods so every household would inspect one another.

sentences.zh: 儉諫曰：「京師翼翼，四方是湊，必也持符，於事既煩，理成不曠，謝安所謂'不爾何以為京師'。

translations.literal: Jian remonstrated, "The capital stands in awe, the four quarters assemble—if tally-holders are required, the affair becomes burdensome, reason becomes neglected, and Xie An's words apply: 'If not so, how would it be the capital?'
translations.idiomatic: Jian remonstrated, "The capital stands in awe, the four quarters assemble—if tally-holders are required, the affair becomes burdensome, reason becomes neglected—and Xie An's words apply: 'If not so, how would it be the capital?'

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: It was thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: It was thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 是歲，有司奏定郊殷之禮，儉以為宜以今年十月殷祭宗廟，自此以後，五年再殷祭。

translations.literal: That year the officials memorialized to fix the suburban and yin sacrifices; Jian held that this year in the tenth month the ancestral temple should receive the yin sacrifice, and from then on every five years two yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: That year the officials memorialized to fix the suburban and yin sacrifices—Jian held that this year in the tenth month the ancestral temple should receive the yin sacrifice, and from then on every five years two yin sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二年正月上辛，有事南郊，即以其日還祭明堂；

translations.literal: In the second year, on the upper xin day of the first month, the southern suburb was served; on that same day the Bright Hall was also sacrificed;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the upper xin day of the first month, the southern suburb was served—on that same day the Bright Hall was also sacrificed;

sentences.zh: 又用次辛饗祀北郊，而並無配。

translations.literal: on the next xin day the northern suburb was feasted, and there were no paired offerings.
translations.idiomatic: on the next xin day the northern suburb was feasted—and there were no paired offerings.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: This was followed.

sentences.zh: 明年轉左僕射，領選如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Left Vice Director, retaining charge of selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Left Vice Director—retaining charge of selection as before.

sentences.zh: 初，宋明帝紫極殿珠簾綺柱，飾以金玉，江左所未有，高帝欲以其材起宣陽門，儉與褚彥回及叔父僧虔連名表諫，上手詔酬納。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Ming of Song's Purple Pole Hall had pearl curtains and brocade pillars adorned with gold and jade, unknown in the Eastern Jin; the High Emperor wished to use the materials for the Xuanyang Gate; Jian with Chu Yanhui and his uncle Sengqian jointly memorialized in remonstrance, and the emperor replied by edict with thanks.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Ming of Song's Purple Pole Hall had pearl curtains and brocade pillars adorned with gold and jade, unknown in the Eastern Jin—the High Emperor wished to use the materials for the Xuanyang Gate—Jian with Chu Yanhui and his uncle Sengqian jointly memorialized in remonstrance, and the emperor replied by edict with thanks.

sentences.zh: 宋世，宮門外六門城設竹籬，是年初，有發白虎樽言：「白門三重門，竹籬穿不完」。

translations.literal: In Song times outside the palace's six gates the city had bamboo fences; at the beginning of that year someone opened the White Tiger casket saying, "White Gate triple gate, bamboo fence pierced incomplete."
translations.idiomatic: In Song times outside the palace's six gates the city had bamboo fences—at the beginning of that year someone opened the White Tiger casket saying, "White Gate triple gate, bamboo fence pierced incomplete."

sentences.zh: 上感其言，改立都牆。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by the words and changed to erect capital walls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would later be moved by the words and changed to erect capital walls.

sentences.zh: 儉又諫，上答曰：「吾欲後世無以加也。

translations.literal: Jian again remonstrated; the emperor replied, "I wish that later ages have nothing to add.
translations.idiomatic: Jian again remonstrated—the emperor replied, "I wish that later ages have nothing to add.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷初基，制度草創，儉問無不決。

translations.literal: When the court was first established and institutions were newly created, there was nothing Jian was asked that he did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: When the court would later be first established and institutions were newly created, there was nothing Jian was asked that he did not decide.

sentences.zh: 上每曰：「詩雲'惟嶽降神，生甫及申'，今天為我生儉也。

translations.literal: The emperor often said, "The Ode says 'Only the mountain sends down spirit, born Fu and Shen'—Heaven has today born Jian for me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often replied, "The Ode says 'Only the mountain sends down spirit, born Fu and Shen'—Heaven has today born Jian for me.

sentences.zh: 」其年固請解選，見許。

translations.literal: That year he firmly requested to relinquish selection and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year he firmly requested to relinquish selection and would later be permitted.

sentences.zh: 帝幸樂遊宴集，謂儉曰：「卿好音樂，孰與朕同？

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Joyful Excursion for a banquet and said to Jian, "You love music—who matches me?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the Joyful Excursion for a banquet and told Jian, "You love music—who matches me?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「沐浴唐風，事兼比屋，亦既在齊，不知肉味。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Bathing in Tang wind, the affair reaches every house; already in Qi, I no longer know the taste of meat.
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "Bathing in Tang wind, the affair reaches every house; already in Qi, I no longer know the taste of meat.

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this.

sentences.zh: 後幸華林宴集，使各效伎藝。

translations.literal: Later at a Huagrove banquet he had each display his skill.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: later at a Huagrove banquet he had each display his skill.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回彈琵琶，王僧虔、柳世隆彈琴，沈文季歌子夜來，張敬兒舞。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui played pipa, Wang Sengqian and Liu Shilong played zither, Shen Wenji sang Ziye Lai, Zhang Jing'er danced.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui played pipa—Wang Sengqian and Liu Shilong played zither, Shen Wenji sang Ziye Lai, Zhang Jing'er danced.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「臣無所解，唯知誦書。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Your minister understands nothing—only knows recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "Your minister understands nothing—only knows recitation.

sentences.zh: 」因跪上前誦相如封禪書。

translations.literal: He then knelt before the emperor and recited Sima Xiangru's Fengshan shu.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he then knelt before the emperor and recited Sima Xiangru's Fengshan shu.

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「此盛德之事，吾何以堪之。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said, "This is a matter of great virtue—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and replied, "This is a matter of great virtue—I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 」後上使陸澄誦孝經，起自「仲尼居」，儉曰：「澄所謂博而寡要。

translations.literal: Later the emperor had Lu Cheng recite the Classic of Filial Piety, beginning from 'Zhongni ju'; Jian said, "What Cheng speaks is broad but lacks essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor had Lu Cheng recite the Classic of Filial Piety, beginning from 'Zhongni ju'; Jian replied, "What Cheng speaks is broad but lacks essentials.

sentences.zh: 臣請誦之。

translations.literal: Your minister asks to recite.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: your minister asks to recite.

sentences.zh: 」乃誦君子之事上章。

translations.literal: He then recited the chapter on the gentleman's service of superiors.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he then recited the chapter on the gentleman's service of superiors.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善，張子布更覺非奇也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good—Zhang Zibu seems even less remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Good—Zhang Zibu seems even less remarkable.

sentences.zh: 」於是王敬則脫朝服袒，以絳糾髻，奮臂拍張，叫動左右。

translations.literal: Then Wang Jingze stripped his court robe bare, bound his hair with crimson cord, swung his arms and beat the drum, shouting and moving those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Jingze stripped his court robe bare—bound his hair with crimson cord, swung his arms and beat the drum, shouting and moving those around him.

sentences.zh: 上不悅曰：「豈聞三公如此。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said, "Have you ever heard of a Three Excellencies doing this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and replied, "Have you ever heard of a Three Excellencies doing this?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「臣以拍張，故得三公，不可忘拍張。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your minister, because of beating the drum, obtained the rank of Three Excellencies—one cannot forget beating the drum.
translations.idiomatic: He replied—"Your minister, because of beating the drum, obtained the rank of Three Excellencies—one cannot forget beating the drum.

sentences.zh: 」時以為名答。

translations.literal: At the time this was considered a famous reply.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, this was considered a famous reply.

sentences.zh: 儉尋以本官領太子詹事，加兵三百人。

translations.literal: Jian soon held his original office concurrently as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with three hundred additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: jian soon held his original office concurrently as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, with three hundred additional troops.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子妃薨，左衛將軍沈文季經為宮臣，未詳服不。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince's consort died; General of the Left Guard Shen Wenji had once been a palace officer and it was unclear whether mourning dress was required.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the crown prince's consort died; General of the Left Guard Shen Wenji had once been a palace officer and it was unclear whether mourning dress was required.

sentences.zh: 儉議曰：「漢、魏以來，宮僚先備臣隸之節，具體在三。

translations.literal: Jian argued, "From Han and Wei onward, palace aides first possessed the protocol of minister and servant; the substance lies in the three relationships.
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued, "From Han and Wei onward, palace aides first possessed the protocol of minister and servant—the substance lies in the three relationships.

sentences.zh: 存既盡敬，亡豈無服？

translations.literal: While alive one shows full reverence—when dead can there be no mourning?
translations.idiomatic: If in life one shows full reverence, in death how can there be no mourning?

sentences.zh: 昔庾翼喪妻，王允、滕含猶謂府吏宜有小君之服，況臣節之重。

translations.literal: In old times when Yu Yi mourned his wife, Wang Yun and Teng Han still held that office clerks should wear the lesser consort's mourning; how much more the weight of ministerial protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In old times when Yu Yi mourned his wife, Wang Yun and Teng Han still held that office clerks should wear the lesser consort's mourning—how much more the weight of ministerial protocol.

sentences.zh: 宜依禮為舊君之妻齊衰三月而除。

translations.literal: One should follow ritual and wear qi mourning for three months for the former lord's wife, then remove it.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: one should follow ritual and wear qi mourning for three months for the former lord's wife, then remove it.

sentences.zh: 」上崩，遺詔以儉為侍中、尚書令、鎮軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the testamentary edict made Jian Palace Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing, and General Who Stabilizes the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the testamentary edict made Jian Palace Attendant, Director of the Masters of Writing—and General Who Stabilizes the Army.

sentences.zh: 每上朝，令史恒有三五十人隨上，諮事辯析，未嘗壅滯。

translations.literal: Each time he attended court, thirty or fifty clerks constantly followed the emperor, consulting and analyzing affairs without ever blocking or delay.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he attended court—thirty or fifty clerks constantly followed the emperor, consulting and analyzing affairs without ever blocking or delay.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回時為司徒、錄尚書，笑謂儉曰：「觀令判斷甚樂。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui was then Minister of Education and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he smiled and said to Jian, "Observing the Director's judgments is great pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui was then Minister of Education and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he smiled and told Jian, "Observing the Director's judgments is great pleasure.

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「所以得厝私懷，實由稟明公不言之化。

translations.literal: Jian said, "The reason I can set private concerns aside is truly because I received Lord Ming's unspoken transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "The reason I can set private concerns aside is truly because I received Lord Ming's unspoken transformation.

sentences.zh: 」武帝即位，給班劍二十人，進號衛將軍，掌選事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu acceded he was given twenty ceremonial swords, promoted to General of the Guard, and held charge of selection.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu acceded he was given twenty ceremonial swords, promoted to General of the Guard—and held charge of selection.

sentences.zh: 時有司以前代嗣位，或仍前郊年，或別為郊始，晉、宋以來，未有畫一。

translations.literal: At the time the officials, regarding former dynasties' succession, either continued the previous suburban year or made a separate beginning for suburban rites; from Jin and Song onward there had been no uniform rule.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the officials, regarding former dynasties' succession, either continued the previous suburban year or made a separate beginning for suburban rites; from Jin and Song onward there had been no uniform rule.

sentences.zh: 儉議曰：「晉明帝太寧三年南郊，其年九月崩；

translations.literal: Jian argued, "Emperor Ming of Jin in the third year of Taining served the southern suburb; that year in the ninth month he died;
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued, "Emperor Ming of Jin in Taining 3 served the southern suburb; that year in the ninth month he died;

sentences.zh: 成帝即位，明年改元，亦郊。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng acceded; the next year he changed the era name and also performed suburban rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng acceded—the next year he changed the era name and also performed suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 簡文咸安二年南郊，其年七月崩；

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen in the second year of Xian'an served the southern suburb; that year in the seventh month he died;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen in Xian'an 2 served the southern suburb; that year in the seventh month he died;

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，明年改元，亦郊。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu acceded; the next year he changed the era name and also performed suburban rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu acceded—the next year he changed the era name and also performed suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉三十年正月南郊，二月崩；

translations.literal: Song in the thirtieth year of Yuanjia in the first month served the southern suburb; in the second month he died;
translations.idiomatic: Song in Yuanjia 30 in the first month served the southern suburb; in the second month he died;

sentences.zh: 孝武嗣位，明年亦郊。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu succeeded; the next year also performed suburban rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu succeeded—the next year also performed suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 此二代明例，差可依放。

translations.literal: These two dynasties are clear examples and may be followed with slight variation.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: these two dynasties are clear examples and may be followed with slight variation.

sentences.zh: 今聖明系業，幽顯宅心，言化則頻郊非嫌，語事則元號初改，禋燎登配，孝敬兼遂。

translations.literal: Now the sage brightness continues the enterprise; hidden and manifest dwell in the heart; speaking of transformation, frequent suburban rites are no offense; speaking of affairs, the era name is newly changed, the sacred fire ascends with paired offerings, filial reverence achieved together.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sage brightness continues the enterprise—hidden and manifest dwell in the heart—speaking of transformation, frequent suburban rites are no offense—speaking of affairs, the era name is newly changed, the sacred fire ascends with paired offerings, filial reverence achieved together.

sentences.zh: 謂明年正月宜饗祀二郊，虔祭明堂。

translations.literal: I hold that next year in the first month both suburbs should be feasted and the Bright Hall reverently sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: i hold that next year in the first month both suburbs should be feasted and the Bright Hall reverently sacrificed.

sentences.zh: 自茲以後，依舊間歲。

translations.literal: From then on, follow the former interval of years.
translations.idiomatic: From then on—follow the former interval of years.

sentences.zh: 」有司又以明年正月上辛應南郊，而立春在上辛後，郊在立春前為疑。

translations.literal: The officials also held that next year on the upper xin day of the first month the southern suburb should be served, but Establishment of Spring fell after the upper xin day, raising doubt that the suburb came before Establishment of Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The officials also held that next year on the upper xin day of the first month the southern suburb should be served—but Establishment of Spring fell after the upper xin day, raising doubt that the suburb came before Establishment of Spring.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「宋景平元年正月三日辛丑南郊，其月十一日立春，元嘉十六年正月六日辛未南郊，其月八日立春，此近世明例也。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Song in the first year of Jingping on the third day of the first month, xinchou, served the southern suburb; on the eleventh day of that month was Establishment of Spring; in the sixteenth year of Yuanjia on the sixth day of the first month, xinwei, served the southern suburb; on the eighth day of that month was Establishment of Spring—these are clear examples of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Song in Jingping 1 on the third day of the first month, xinchou, served the southern suburb; on the eleventh day of that month was Establishment of Spring; in Yuanjia 16 on the sixth day of the first month, xinwei, served the southern suburb; on the eighth day of that month was Establishment of Spring—these are clear examples of recent times.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All were followed.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，領丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he held Danyang concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 2 he held Danyang concurrently.

sentences.zh: 三年，領國子祭酒，又領太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the third year he held Director of the National University concurrently and also Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: in the third year he held Director of the National University concurrently and also Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 舊太子敬二傅同，至是朝議接少傅以賓友禮。

translations.literal: Formerly the heir's reverence toward both tutors was the same; from this time court deliberation treated the Junior Tutor with guest-friend ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the heir's reverence toward both tutors was the same—from this time court deliberation treated the Junior Tutor with guest-friend ritual.

sentences.zh: 宋時國學頹廢，未暇修復，宋明帝泰始六年，置總明觀以集學士，或謂之東觀，置東觀祭酒一人，總明訪舉郎二人；

translations.literal: In Song times the National University had fallen into ruin and there was no leisure to restore it; in the sixth year of Taishi of Emperor Ming of Song the Zongming Observatory was established to gather scholars, also called the Eastern Observatory, with one Director of the Eastern Observatory and two Zongming Recommendation Officers;
translations.idiomatic: In Song times the National University had fallen into ruin and there was no leisure to restore it; in Taishi 6 of Emperor Ming of Song the Zongming Observatory was established to gather scholars, also called the Eastern Observatory, with one Director of the Eastern Observatory and two Zongming Recommendation Officers;

sentences.zh: 儒、玄、文、史四科，科置學士十人，其餘令史以下各有差。

translations.literal: Confucian, Mystery, Letters, and History four sections, each section ten scholars, the rest clerks and below each with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian, Mystery, Letters—and History four sections, each section ten scholars, the rest clerks and below each with differences.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以國學既立，省總明觀，於儉宅開學士館，以總明四部書充之。

translations.literal: That year, because the National University was established, the Zongming Observatory was abolished; at Jian's residence a Scholars' Hall was opened, filled with the Zongming four-division books.
translations.idiomatic: That year, because the National University was established, the Zongming Observatory was abolished—at Jian's residence a Scholars' Hall was opened, filled with the Zongming four-division books.

sentences.zh: 又詔儉以家為府。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Jian to use his house as an office.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: the emperor also ordered Jian to use his house as an office.

sentences.zh: 四年，以本官領吏部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he held his original office concurrently as Director of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: in the fourth year he held his original office concurrently as Director of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是宋孝武好文章，天下悉以文采相尚，莫以專經為業。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Xiaowu of Song loved literary composition; the realm all took literary elegance as fashion and none made classical learning their profession.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Xiaowu of Song loved literary composition—the realm all took literary elegance as fashion and none made classical learning their profession.

sentences.zh: 儉弱年便留意三禮，尤善春秋，發言吐論，造次必於儒教，由是衣冠翕然，並尚經學，儒教於此大興。

translations.literal: From youth Jian attended to the three rites and especially excelled in Spring and Autumn; in speech and debate he always adhered to Confucian teaching even in haste—thereupon the gentry converged and all honored classical learning, and Confucian teaching greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood, Jian attended to the three rites and especially excelled in Spring and Autumn; in speech and debate he always adhered to Confucian teaching even in haste—thereupon the gentry converged and all honored classical learning, and Confucian teaching greatly flourished.

sentences.zh: 何承天禮論三百卷，儉抄為八帙，又別抄條目為十三卷。

translations.literal: He Chengtian's Ritual Discussions in three hundred scrolls Jian abridged into eight fascicles and separately abridged entries into thirteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian's Ritual Discussions ran three hundred scrolls; Jian abridged them into eight fascicles and separately copied out entries into thirteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 朝儀舊典，晉、宋來施行故事，撰次諳憶，無遺漏者。

translations.literal: Court ritual and old regulations, Jin and Song precedents carried out in practice—he compiled and remembered them without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual and old regulations—Jin and Song precedents carried out in practice—he compiled and remembered them without omission.

sentences.zh: 所以當朝理事，斷決如流。

translations.literal: Therefore in governing the court his decisions flowed like water.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: therefore in governing the court his decisions flowed like water.

sentences.zh: 每博議引證，先儒罕有其例，八坐丞郎，無能異者。

translations.literal: Each time in broad deliberation he cited proof; former scholars rarely had his examples, and none among the eight seats and director clerks could differ.
translations.idiomatic: Each time in broad deliberation he cited proof—former scholars rarely had his examples, and none among the eight seats and director clerks could differ.

sentences.zh: 令史諮事，賓客滿席，儉應接銓序，傍無留滯。

translations.literal: When clerks consulted on affairs and guests filled the hall, Jian received and arranged them in sequence with none left waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks consulted on affairs and guests filled the hall—Jian received and arranged them in sequence with none left waiting.

sentences.zh: 十日一還，監試諸生，巾卷在庭，劍衛令史，儀容甚盛。

translations.literal: Every ten days he returned once, supervised examination of students; scrolls in the courtyard, sword guards and order clerks—the bearing was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten days he returned once, supervised examination of students—scrolls in the courtyard, sword guards and order clerks—the bearing was very grand.

sentences.zh: 作解散幘，斜插簪，朝野慕之，相與放效。

translations.literal: He made a loose headband and slanted the hairpin; court and realm admired it and imitated one another.
translations.idiomatic: He made a loose headband and slanted the hairpin—court and realm admired it and imitated one another.

sentences.zh: 儉常謂人曰，「江左風流宰相，惟有謝安」，蓋自況也。

translations.literal: Jian often said to people, "Among elegant chancellors of the Eastern Jin there was only Xie An"—he was comparing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jian often told people, "Among elegant chancellors of the Eastern Jin there was only Xie An"—he was comparing himself.

sentences.zh: 武帝深委仗之，士流選用，奏無不可。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply relied on him; in selecting men of the gentry, none of his memorials was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu deeply relied on him—in selecting men of the gentry, none of his memorials was denied.

sentences.zh: 儉寡嗜欲，唯以經國為務，車服塵素，家無遺財。

translations.literal: Jian had few desires and took governing the state as his task; carriage and dress were dusty and plain, and the house held no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had few desires and took governing the state as his task—carriage and dress were dusty and plain, and the house held no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 手筆典裁，為當時所重。

translations.literal: His own hand in drafting and judgment was valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His own hand in drafting and judgment would later be valued by the age.

sentences.zh: 少便有宰臣之志，賦詩云：「稷契匡虞夏，伊呂翼商周。

translations.literal: From youth he had the ambition of a chief minister; in a poem he wrote, "Ji and Qi upheld Yu and Xia; Yi and Lü winged Shang and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood, he had the ambition of a chief minister; in a poem he wrote, "Ji and Qi upheld Yu and Xia; Yi and Lü winged Shang and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」及生子，字曰玄成，取仍世作相之義。

translations.literal: When he had a son he styled him Xuancheng, taking the meaning of generation after generation as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he had a son he styled him Xuancheng—taking the meaning of generation after generation as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 撰古今喪服集記並文集，並行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Records of Mourning Dress Ancient and Modern and collected writings, both circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Records of Mourning Dress Ancient and Modern and collected writings, both of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝受禪，詔為儉立碑，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang received the abdication, he ordered a stele erected for Jian and lowered his rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang received the abdication—he ordered a stele erected for Jian and lowered his rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 儉弟遜，宋升明中為丹陽丞，告劉彥節事，不蒙封賞。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Xun in Song's Shengming served as Assistant Governor of Danyang and reported Liu Yanjie's affair, but received no enfeoffment or reward.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Xun in Song's Shengming served as Assistant Governor of Danyang and reported Liu Yanjie's affair—but received no enfeoffment or reward.

sentences.zh: 建元初，為晉陵太守，有怨言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was Governor of Jinling and had resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyuan he would later be Governor of Jinling and had resentful words.

sentences.zh: 儉慮為禍，因褚彥回啟聞，中丞陸澄依事舉奏。

translations.literal: Jian feared it would bring disaster and through Chu Yanhui reported it; Censor-in-Chief Lu Cheng memorialized according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Jian feared it would bring disaster and through Chu Yanhui reported it—Censor-in-Chief Lu Cheng memorialized according to the facts.

sentences.zh: 詔以儉竭誠佐命，特降刑書宥遜，遠徙永嘉郡，於道伏誅。

translations.literal: An edict said that because Jian had exhausted himself aiding the mandate, Xun was specially pardoned by written sentence and exiled far to Yongjia commandery; on the road he was executed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said that because Jian had exhausted himself aiding the mandate, Xun was specially pardoned by written sentence and exiled far to Yongjia commandery—on the road he was executed in secret.

sentences.zh: 長子騫嗣。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: his eldest son Qian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 騫字思寂，本字玄成，與齊高帝偏諱同，故改焉。

translations.literal: Qian, styled Siji, originally styled Xuancheng; because it matched the taboo of Emperor Gao of Qi's personal name, it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, courtesy name Siji, originally styled Xuancheng; because it matched the taboo of Emperor Gao of Qi's personal name, it was changed.

sentences.zh: 性凝簡，慕樂廣為人，未嘗言人之短。

translations.literal: By nature he was reserved and plain, admired Yue Guang's character, and never spoke of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was reserved and plain, admired Yue Guang's character—and never spoke of others' faults.

sentences.zh: 諸女子侄皆嬪王尚主，朔望來歸，輜軿填咽，非所欲也，敕歲中不過一再見。

translations.literal: All his daughters and nephews married princes or princesses; on the first and fifteenth they came home, carriages filling the road—not what he wished; he ordered that in a year they should meet no more than once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: All his daughters and nephews married princes or princesses—on the first and fifteenth they came home, carriages filling the road—not what he wished—he ordered that in a year they should meet no more than once or twice.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容謂諸子曰：「吾家本素族，自可依流平進，不須苟求也。

translations.literal: He once said at ease to his sons, "Our house is originally a plain clan; one may rely on gradual advancement in the stream—there is no need to grasp greedily.
translations.idiomatic: He once said at ease to his sons, "Our house is originally a plain clan—one may rely on gradual advancement in the stream—there is no need to grasp greedily.

sentences.zh: 」曆黃門郎、司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He served as Palace Secretary, Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Secretary—Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 不事產業，有舊墅在鍾山八十餘頃，與諸宅及故舊共佃之。

translations.literal: He did not manage property; there was an old villa at Zhongshan of more than eighty qing, which he shared in tenancy with various residences and old friends.

translations.idiomatic: He often told people, "I am not like Lord Zheng, who had four hundred qing of fields yet often lacked enough to eat.

translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the abdication his enfeoffment would later be lowered to marquis.

translations.idiomatic: He held a succession of posts: Minister of Revenue, Palace Secretary.

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu built the Great Ai'jing Temple west of Zhongshan—Qian's old villa beside the temple was the field Wang Dao had been granted.

translations.literal: He replied, "This field is not for sale;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "This land is not for sale;

sentences.zh: 」酬對又脫略。

translations.idiomatic: In sum: his replies were also blunt and brief.

translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and then had the market assess the field price and return it to him at full value.

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨，出為吳興太守。

translations.idiomatic: On this account he offended the emperor and would later be sent out as Governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 騫性侈於味而儉於服，頗以多忌為累。

sentences.zh: 又惰於接物，雖主書宣敕，或過時不見。

translations.idiomatic: He was also slack in receiving people—even when chief clerks announced edicts he sometimes would not see them for a long time.

sentences.zh: 才望不及弟暕，特以儉之嫡，故不棄于時。

translations.idiomatic: His talent and standing did not match his younger brother Yan's—yet because he was Jian's legitimate son he was not cast aside by the age.

translations.idiomatic: Yan was Left Vice Director and Vice Director in charge of the court—Qian went from Palace Secretary to a commandery, discontent and unhappy, and in the commandery lay abed and ignored affairs.

translations.idiomatic: He would later be recalled as Minister of Revenue with Supervising Director added, holding concurrently Commandant of the Archers.

translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰安。

sentences.zh: 子規。

translations.idiomatic: His son was Gui.

translations.idiomatic: Gui, courtesy name Weiming, at eight entered mourning for his birth mother and in mourning showed utmost nature.

translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Xu Xiaosi of Qi wept every time he saw the boy and named him "Filial Youth."

translations.idiomatic: He would later be made Reception Chief Clerk of his native province.

translations.literal: He began office as Secretary, rose through appointments to Heir Apparent Purifier.
translations.idiomatic: He began office as Secretary—rose through appointments to Heir Apparent Purifier.

sentences.zh: 天監十二年，改造太極殿畢，規獻新殿賦，其辭甚工。

translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian 12, when reconstruction of the Taichi Hall was completed, Gui presented a rhapsody on the new hall; the wording was very skilled.

translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Adviser to Prince of Jin'an Gang, Cloud-Banner General; after long service he was Governor of Xin'an.

translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of his father's mourning; when mourning ended he inherited the marquisate of Nanchang.

translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangdong Yi was then Governor of Danyang—at a banquet with court gentlemen he assigned Gui as wine-master.

translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Chief Secretary to Prince of Jin'an.

translations.idiomatic: At this time Zhenzong took leave to return—Gui treated him very coldly—Zhenzong returned to the capital and secretly memorialized that Gui did not govern commandery affairs.

translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made recalled as Minister of the Left Household.

translations.idiomatic: Cheng, courtesy name Anqi, at first was Secretary; he rose through appointments to Palace Secretary and Yellow Gate Attendant, concurrently National University Erudite.
