translations.literal: He died in the commandery; his posthumous title was Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the commandery—his posthumous title was Zhang.

sentences.zh: 承性簡貴，有風格。

translations.literal: Cheng by nature was plain and noble, with bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng by nature was plain and noble—with bearing.

sentences.zh: 右衛朱異當朝用事，每休下，車馬填門。

translations.literal: Right Guard Zhu Yi held power in the court; each time he left office carriages and horses filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard Zhu Yi held power in the court—each time he left office carriages and horses filled his gate.

sentences.zh: 有魏郡申英者，門寒才俊，好危言高論以忤權右。

translations.literal: There was Shen Ying of Wei commandery, from a cold gate yet talented and handsome, who loved stern words and lofty discourse to offend the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: There was Shen Ying of Wei commandery—from a cold gate yet talented and handsome, who loved stern words and lofty discourse to offend the powerful.

sentences.zh: 嘗指異門曰：「此中輻湊，皆為利往，能不至者，唯大小王東陽耳。

translations.literal: He once pointed at Yi's gate and said, "Within this hub all go for profit; those who can fail to come are only the two Wangs of Dongyang, great and small.
translations.idiomatic: He once pointed at Yi's gate and replied, "Within this hub all go for profit; those who can fail to come are only the two Wangs of Dongyang, great and small.

sentences.zh: 」小東陽即承弟幼也。

translations.literal: Small Dongyang was Cheng's younger brother You.
translations.idiomatic: Small Dongyang would later be Cheng's younger brother You.

sentences.zh: 時唯承兄弟及褚翔不至異門，世並稱之。

translations.literal: At the time only the Cheng brothers and Chu Xiang did not come to Yi's gate; the world together praised them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, only the Cheng brothers and Chu Xiang did not come to Yi's gate; the world together praised them.

sentences.zh: 訓字懷範，生而紫胞，師媼云：「法當貴」。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Huaifan, was born with a purple birth-caul; the midwife said, "By rule he should be noble."
translations.idiomatic: Xun, courtesy name Huaifan, was born with a purple birth-caul; the midwife said, "By rule he should be noble."

sentences.zh: 幼聰警，有識量，僧正惠超見而奇之，謂門人羅智國曰：「四郎眉目疏朗，舉動和韻，此是興門戶者。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and alert with judgment; Abbot Huichao of the Sangha saw him and marveled, telling his disciple Luo Zhiguo, "The fourth lord's brows and eyes are open and clear, his movements harmonious—this one will raise the gate.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood, he was clever and alert with judgment; Abbot Huichao of the Sangha saw him and marveled, telling his disciple Luo Zhiguo, "The fourth lord's brows and eyes are open and clear, his movements harmonious—this one will raise the gate.

sentences.zh: 」智國以白暕，暕亦曰：「不墜基業，其在文殊。

translations.literal: Zhiguo told Yan; Yan also said, "He will not fall from the foundation—it is Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiguo told Yan; Yan also replied, "He will not fall from the foundation—it is Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 」文殊，訓小字也。

translations.literal: Wenshu was Xun's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu would later be Xun's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 年十三，暕亡，憂毀，家人莫識。

translations.literal: At thirteen Yan died; in grief and ruin his family did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Yan died—in grief and ruin his family did not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 十六召見文德殿，應對爽徹，上目送久之，謂朱異曰：「可謂相門有相。

translations.literal: At sixteen he was summoned to Wende Hall; his replies were clear and penetrating; the emperor saw him off with his gaze a long while and said to Zhu Yi, "One may say the minister's gate has a minister.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was summoned to Wende Hall; his replies were clear and penetrating; the emperor saw him off with his gaze a long while and told Zhu Yi, "One may say the minister's gate has a minister.

sentences.zh: 」初補國子生，問說師袁昂。

translations.literal: At first he was supplemented as National University student and questioned Lecturer Yuan Ang.
translations.idiomatic: At first he would later be supplemented as National University student and questioned Lecturer Yuan Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂曰：「久籍高名，有勞虛想，及觀容止，若披雲霧。

translations.literal: Ang said, "Long have I known your lofty name and labored in vain imagination; now seeing your bearing and stop, it is like parting clouds and mist.
translations.idiomatic: Ang replied, "Long have I known your lofty name and labored in vain imagination; now seeing your bearing and stop, it is like parting clouds and mist.

sentences.zh: 」俄而諸袁子弟來，昂謂諸助教曰：「我兒出十數，若有一子如此，實無所恨。

translations.literal: Soon the various Yuan sons and nephews came; Ang told the various assistants, "My sons come by the tens; if one son were like this, I would truly have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the various Yuan sons and nephews came—Ang told the various assistants, "My sons come by the tens—if one son were like this, I would truly have no regret.

sentences.zh: 」射策，除秘書郎，累遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: In the archery examination he was made Secretary; he rose through appointments to Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the archery examination he was made Secretary—he rose through appointments to Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 嘗賦詩云：「旦奭匡世功，蕭曹佐甿俗。

translations.literal: He once composed a poem saying, "Dan and Shi upheld the age's merit; Xiao and Cao assisted the people's customs.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed a poem saying, "Dan and Shi upheld the age's merit—Xiao and Cao assisted the people's customs.

sentences.zh: 」追祖儉之志也。

translations.literal: He traced his ancestor Jian's ambition.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he traced his ancestor Jian's ambition.

sentences.zh: 後拜侍中，入見武帝。

translations.literal: Later he was made Palace Attendant and entered audience with Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed made Palace Attendant and entered audience with Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝問何敬容曰：「褚彥回年幾為宰相？

translations.literal: The emperor asked He Jingrong, "At what age did Chu Yanhui become chief minister?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked He Jingrong—"At what age did Chu Yanhui become chief minister?

sentences.zh: 」敬容曰：「少過三十。

translations.literal: Jingrong said, "A little past thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong replied, "A little past thirty.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「今之王訓，無謝彥回。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Today's Wang Xun is not inferior to Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Today's Wang Xun is not inferior to Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 」訓美容儀，善進止，文章為後進領袖。

translations.literal: Xun's appearance was beautiful, his advance and stop skilled; his literary compositions led the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's appearance was beautiful, his advance and stop skilled—his literary compositions led the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 年二十六，卒，諡溫子。

translations.literal: At twenty-six he died; his posthumous title was Wenzi.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-six he died—his posthumous title was Wenzi.

sentences.zh: 僧虔，金紫光祿大夫僧綽弟也。

translations.literal: Sengqian was younger brother of Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Sengchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian would later be younger brother of Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Sengchuo.

sentences.zh: 父曇首，與兄弟集會子孫，任其戲適。

translations.literal: His father Tanshou, with his brothers gathering descendants, let them play as they wished.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanshou—with his brothers gathering descendants, let them play as they wished.

sentences.zh: 僧達跳下地作彪子。

translations.literal: Sengda jumped to the ground and played leopard cub.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: sengda jumped to the ground and played leopard cub.

sentences.zh: 時僧虔累十二博棋，既不墜落，亦不重作。

translations.literal: At the time Sengqian had piled twelve go pieces; they neither fell nor were reset.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Sengqian had piled twelve go pieces; they neither fell nor were reset.

sentences.zh: 僧綽采蠟燭珠為鳳皇，僧達奪取打壞，亦復不惜。

translations.literal: Sengchuo gathered wax candle pearls into a phoenix; Sengda snatched and smashed it, yet Sengchuo did not regret.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo gathered wax candle pearls into a phoenix—Sengda snatched and smashed it, yet Sengchuo did not regret.

sentences.zh: 伯父弘歎曰：「僧達俊爽，當不減人；

translations.literal: Uncle Hong sighed and said, "Sengda is handsome and bright and will not fall short of others;
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Hong sighed and replied, "Sengda is handsome and bright and will not fall short of others;

sentences.zh: 然亡吾家者，終此子也。

translations.literal: yet the one who will destroy our house will ultimately be this boy.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: yet the one who will destroy our house will ultimately be this boy.

sentences.zh: 僧虔必至公，僧綽當以名義見美。

translations.literal: Sengqian will surely reach public office; Sengchuo will be praised for righteousness and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian will surely reach public office—Sengchuo will be praised for righteousness and reputation.

sentences.zh: 」或云僧虔采燭珠為鳳皇，弘稱其長者云。

translations.literal: Some say Sengqian gathered candle pearls into a phoenix and Hong praised his elder conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: some say Sengqian gathered candle pearls into a phoenix and Hong praised his elder conduct.

sentences.zh: 僧虔弱冠，雅善隸書，宋文帝見其書素扇，歎曰：「非唯跡逾子敬，方當器雅過之。

translations.literal: At weak crown Sengqian excelled at clerical script; Emperor Wen of Song saw his writing on a plain fan and sighed, "Not only does the trace surpass Zijing—the bearing in elegance will surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: At weak crown Sengqian excelled at clerical script—Emperor Wen of Song saw his writing on a plain fan and sighed, "Not only does the trace surpass Zijing—the bearing in elegance will surpass him.

sentences.zh: 」為太子舍人，退默少交接。

translations.literal: He was Attendant of the Heir Apparent, retiring and silent with little social contact.
translations.idiomatic: He was Attendant of the Heir Apparent—retiring and silent with little social contact.

sentences.zh: 與袁淑、謝莊善，淑每歎之曰：「卿文情鴻麗，學解深拔，而韜光潛實，物莫之窺，雖魏陽元之射，王汝南之騎，無以加焉。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Yuan Shu and Xie Zhuang; Shu often sighed over him and said, "Your literary feeling is grand and beautiful, learning and understanding deeply pulled forth, yet you hide your light and bury your substance—nothing penetrates to view; though Wei Yangyuan's archery and Wang Runan's horsemanship cannot surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Yuan Shu and Xie Zhuang; Shu often sighed over him and replied, "Your literary feeling is grand and beautiful, learning and understanding deeply pulled forth, yet you hide your light and bury your substance—nothing penetrates to view; though Wei Yangyuan's archery and Wang Runan's horsemanship cannot surpass this.

sentences.zh: 」遷司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Western Aide of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Western Aide of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 兄僧綽為宋元凶所害，親賓咸勸之逃，僧虔泣曰：「吾兄奉國以忠貞，撫我以慈愛，今日之事，苦不見及耳。

translations.literal: When elder brother Sengchuo was killed by Song's crown prince the villain, kin and guests all urged him to flee; Sengqian wept and said, "My elder brother served the state with loyalty and nurtured me with kindness—today's affair, I bitterly did not reach it in time.
translations.idiomatic: When elder brother Sengchuo was killed by Song's crown prince the villain, kin and guests all urged him to flee; Sengqian wept and replied, "My elder brother served the state with loyalty and nurtured me with kindness—today's affair, I bitterly did not reach it in time.

sentences.zh: 若同歸九泉，猶羽化也。

translations.literal: If we go together to the nine springs, it is still transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If we go together to the nine springs—it is still transformation.

sentences.zh: 」孝武初，出為武陵太守，攜諸子侄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu he went out as Governor of Wuling, taking sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu he went out as Governor of Wuling, taking sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 兄子儉中塗得病，僧虔為廢寢食，同行客慰喻之。

translations.literal: Nephew Jian fell ill midway; Sengqian for him abandoned sleep and food; fellow travelers consoled him.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Jian fell ill midway—Sengqian for him abandoned sleep and food—fellow travelers consoled him.

sentences.zh: 僧虔曰：「昔馬援處子侄之間，一情不異，鄧攸于弟子，更逾所生，吾實懷其心，誠未異古。

translations.literal: Sengqian said, "In old times Ma Yuan among sons and nephews felt one emotion without difference; Deng You toward his younger brother's son exceeded what he bore himself—I truly hold that heart and am truly not different from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian replied, "In old times Ma Yuan among sons and nephews felt one emotion without difference; Deng You toward his younger brother's son exceeded what he bore himself—I truly hold that heart and am truly not different from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 亡兄之胤，不宜忽諸，若此兒不救，便當回舟謝職。

translations.literal: The deceased elder brother's heir should not be neglected; if this boy is not saved, I shall turn the boat and resign office.
translations.idiomatic: The deceased elder brother's heir should not be neglected—if this boy is not saved, I shall turn the boat and resign office.

sentences.zh: 」還為中書郎，再遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He returned as Palace Secretary, then was transferred twice to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Palace Secretary—then was transferred twice to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 孝武欲擅書名，僧虔不敢顯跡，大明世常用掘筆書，以此見容。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu wished to monopolize the fame of calligraphy; Sengqian dared not show his traces; in the Daming era he commonly used a buried brush to write and thus was tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu wished to monopolize the fame of calligraphy—Sengqian dared not show his traces—in the Daming era he commonly used a buried brush to write and thus was tolerated.

sentences.zh: 後為御史中丞，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was Censor-in-Chief, holding concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Censor-in-Chief, holding concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 甲族由來多不居憲台，王氏分枝居烏衣者，位宦微減。

translations.literal: Noble clans from old rarely held the Inspectorate; the Wang branch dwelling at Wuyi saw office slightly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Noble clans from old rarely held the Inspectorate—the Wang branch dwelling at Wuyi saw office slightly reduced.

sentences.zh: 僧虔為此官，乃曰：「此是烏衣諸郎坐處，我亦可試為耳。

translations.literal: Sengqian in this office then said, "This is where the Wuyi lords sit—I too may try it.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian in this office then replied, "This is where the Wuyi lords sit—I too may try it.

sentences.zh: 」泰始中，為吳興太守。

translations.literal: In Taishi he was Governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi he would later be Governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 始王獻之善書，為吳興郡，及僧虔工書，又為郡，論者稱之。

translations.literal: At first Wang Xianzhi excelled at calligraphy and was Governor of Wuxing; when Sengqian mastered calligraphy he again was governor—commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wang Xianzhi excelled at calligraphy and was Governor of Wuxing—when Sengqian mastered calligraphy he again was governor—commentators praised this.

sentences.zh: 徙會稽太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人阮佃夫家在東，請假歸，客勸僧虔以佃夫要幸，宜加禮接。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Ruan Tianfu's family was in the east; he took leave to return and guests urged Sengqian that Tianfu was favored and he should add courteous reception.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Ruan Tianfu's family was in the east—he took leave to return and guests urged Sengqian that Tianfu was favored and he should add courteous reception.

sentences.zh: 僧虔曰：「我立身有素，豈能曲意此輩；

translations.literal: Sengqian said, "I establish myself with constancy—how can I bend intent to this sort?
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian replied, "I establish myself with constancy—how can I bend intent to this sort?

sentences.zh: 彼若見惡，當拂衣去耳。

translations.literal: If he hates me for it, I shall brush my robes and leave.
translations.idiomatic: If he hates me for it—I shall brush my robes and leave.

sentences.zh: 」佃夫言于宋明帝，使御史中丞孫敻奏僧虔，坐免官。

translations.literal: Tianfu spoke to Emperor Ming of Song; he had Censor-in-Chief Sun Xuan memorialize against Sengqian and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu spoke to Emperor Ming of Song—he had Censor-in-Chief Sun Xuan memorialize against Sengqian and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋以白衣領侍中。

translations.literal: Soon in plain clothes he held Palace Attendant concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: soon in plain clothes he held Palace Attendant concurrently.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，為吏部尚書，尋加散騎常侍，轉右僕射。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui he was Minister of the Masters of Writing; soon Attendant Cavalier Regular was added; he was transferred to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui he was Minister of the Masters of Writing—soon Attendant Cavalier Regular was added—he was transferred to Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 升明二年，為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he was Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2 he was Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 嘗為飛白書題尚書省壁曰：「圓行方止，物之定質，修之不已則溢，高之不已則栗，馳之不已則躓，引之不已則疊，是故去之宜疾。

translations.literal: He once wrote in flying-white script on the Masters of Writing wall, "Round goes, square stops—the fixed substance of things; cultivate without cease and it overflows, raise without cease and it shrinks, gallop without cease and you stumble, draw without cease and it piles—therefore remove it swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote in flying-white script on the Masters of Writing wall, "Round goes, square stops—the fixed substance of things—cultivate without cease and it overflows, raise without cease and it shrinks, gallop without cease and you stumble, draw without cease and it piles—therefore remove it swiftly.

sentences.zh: 」當時嗟賞，以比坐右銘。

translations.literal: At the time people sighed in admiration and compared it to a seat-side inscription.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, people sighed in admiration and compared it to a seat-side inscription.

sentences.zh: 兄子儉每覲見，輒勖以前言往行、忠貞止足之道。

translations.literal: Nephew Jian each time he had audience Jian would exhort him with former words and deeds and the way of loyalty, sufficiency, and stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Jian each time he had audience Jian would exhort him with former words and deeds and the way of loyalty, sufficiency—and stopping.

sentences.zh: 雅好文史，解音律，以朝廷禮樂，多違正典，人間競造新聲。

translations.literal: He elegantly loved letters and history, understood pitch and mode; because court ritual and music mostly violated the correct canon, the world competed to make new sounds.
translations.idiomatic: He elegantly loved letters and history, understood pitch and mode—because court ritual and music mostly violated the correct canon, the world competed to make new sounds.

sentences.zh: 時齊高帝輔政，僧虔上表請正聲樂，高帝乃使侍中蕭惠基調正清商音律。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gao of Qi assisted governance; Sengqian memorialized asking to correct music; the High Emperor then had Palace Attendant Xiao Huiji tune and correct Clear Shang pitch and mode.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Emperor Gao of Qi assisted governance; Sengqian memorialized asking to correct music; the High Emperor then had Palace Attendant Xiao Huiji tune and correct Clear Shang pitch and mode.

sentences.zh: 齊受命，轉侍中、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate he was moved to Palace Attendant and Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 郡縣獄相承有上湯殺囚，僧虔上言：「湯本救疾，而實行冤暴，若罪必入重，自有正刑，若去惡宜疾，則應先啟，豈有死生大命，而潛制下邑。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties in prisons inherited applying hot water to kill prisoners; Sengqian memorialized, "Hot water originally saves illness yet in practice becomes wrongful violence; if guilt must enter the heavy, there is the correct punishment; if removing evil should be swift, one should first report—how can there be the great mandate of life and death secretly decided in lower districts?
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and counties in prisons inherited applying hot water to kill prisoners—Sengqian memorialized, "Hot water originally saves illness yet in practice becomes wrongful violence—if guilt must enter the heavy, there is the correct punishment—if removing evil should be swift, one should first report—how can there be the great mandate of life and death secretly decided in lower districts?

sentences.zh: 」上納其言而止。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel and abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子鎮雍州，有盜發古塚者，相傳云是楚王塚，大獲寶物：玉履、玉屏風、竹簡書、青絲綸。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince of Culture and Kindness garrisoned Yong Province, tomb robbers opened an ancient tomb; tradition said it was the tomb of a king of Chu, greatly obtaining treasures: jade shoes, jade screen, bamboo slip books, blue silk cords.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince of Culture and Kindness garrisoned Yong Province, tomb robbers opened an ancient tomb—tradition said it was the tomb of a king of Chu, greatly obtaining treasures: jade shoes, jade screen, bamboo slip books, blue silk cords.

sentences.zh: 簡廣數分，長二尺，皮節如新。

translations.literal: The slips were several fen wide and two chi long; the bark joints were like new.
translations.idiomatic: The slips were several fen wide and two chi long—the bark joints were like new.

sentences.zh: 有得十餘簡以示僧虔，雲是科斗書考工記，周官所闕文也。

translations.literal: More than ten slips were obtained and shown to Sengqian; they said it was tadpole script Records of the Artificer, text the Offices of Zhou lacked.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten slips were obtained and shown to Sengqian—they said it was tadpole script Records of the Artificer, text the Offices of Zhou lacked.

sentences.zh: 高帝素善書，篤好不已，與僧虔賭書畢，謂曰：「誰為第一？

translations.literal: The High Emperor from old excelled at calligraphy and loved it deeply without cease; when he finished betting calligraphy with Sengqian he said to him, "Who is first?
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor from old excelled at calligraphy and loved it deeply without cease; when he finished betting calligraphy with Sengqian he told him, "Who is first?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣書第一，陛下亦第一。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your minister's calligraphy is first; Your Majesty is also first.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your minister's calligraphy is first—Your Majesty is also first.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿可謂善自為謀。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said, "You may be called good at plotting for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and replied, "You may be called good at plotting for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」或云帝問：「我書何如卿？

translations.literal: Some say the emperor asked, "How is my calligraphy compared with yours?
translations.idiomatic: Some say the emperor asked—"How is my calligraphy compared with yours?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「臣正書第一，草書第二；

translations.literal: He replied, "Your minister's regular script is first, cursive script second;
translations.idiomatic: He replied—"Your minister's regular script is first, cursive script second;

sentences.zh: 陛下草書第二，而正書第三。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's cursive script is second, regular script third.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's cursive script is second—regular script third.

sentences.zh: 臣無第三，陛下無第一。

translations.literal: Your minister has no third; Your Majesty has no first.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister has no third—Your Majesty has no first.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑曰：「卿善為辭；

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and said, "You are good at phrasing;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed greatly and replied, "You are good at phrasing;

sentences.zh: 然天下有道，丘不與易也。

translations.literal: yet when the realm has the Way, Qiu would not exchange with him.
translations.idiomatic: yet when the realm has the Way—Qiu would not exchange with him.

sentences.zh: 」帝示僧虔古跡十一卷，就求能書人名。

translations.literal: The emperor showed Sengqian eleven scrolls of ancient traces and asked for the names of able calligraphers.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: the emperor showed Sengqian eleven scrolls of ancient traces and asked for the names of able calligraphers.

sentences.zh: 僧虔得人間所有卷中所無者：吳大皇帝、景帝、歸命侯書，桓玄書，及王丞相導、領軍洽、中書令瑉、張芝、索靖、衛伯儒、張翼十一卷，奏之。

translations.literal: Sengqian obtained what the world's collections lacked in the scrolls: writings of the Great Emperor of Wu, Emperor Jing, Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan's writing, and eleven scrolls of Wang Chancellor Dao, Army Commander Qia, Palace Secretary Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boru, and Zhang Yi, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian obtained what the world's collections lacked in the scrolls: writings of the Great Emperor of Wu, Emperor Jing, Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan's writing—and eleven scrolls of Wang Chancellor Dao, Army Commander Qia, Palace Secretary Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boru, and Zhang Yi, and presented them.

sentences.zh: 又上羊欣所撰能書人名一卷。

translations.literal: He also presented one scroll of Yang Xin's compilation of names of able calligraphers.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he also presented one scroll of Yang Xin's compilation of names of able calligraphers.

sentences.zh: 遷湘州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Xiang Province, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Governor of Xiang Province, Palace Attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 清簡不營財產，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Plain and simple, he did not manage property; the hundred families were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Living plainly, he amassed no property, and the common people lived in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 僧虔論書云：「宋文帝書，自言可比王子敬。

translations.literal: Sengqian's Discourse on Calligraphy says, "Emperor Wen of Song's calligraphy—he himself said it could compare with Wang Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian's Discourse on Calligraphy says—"Emperor Wen of Song's calligraphy—he himself said it could compare with Wang Zijing.

sentences.zh: 時議者雲，'天然勝羊欣，功夫少於欣'。

translations.literal: Commentators of the time said, 'Natural talent surpasses Yang Xin, effort less than Xin.'
translations.idiomatic: Commentators of the time said—'Natural talent surpasses Yang Xin, effort less than Xin.'

sentences.zh: 王平南廙，右軍叔，過江，右軍之前以為最。

translations.literal: Wang Pingnan Yi, the Right General's uncle, crossed the river; before the Right General he was considered best.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pingnan Yi, the Right General's uncle, crossed the river—before the Right General he was considered best.

sentences.zh: 亡曾祖領軍書，右軍云：'弟書遂不減吾。

translations.literal: The deceased great-grandfather Army Commander's calligraphy—the Right General said, 'Younger brother's calligraphy indeed does not diminish mine.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: the deceased great-grandfather Army Commander's calligraphy—the Right General said, 'Younger brother's calligraphy indeed does not diminish mine.

sentences.zh: '變古制，今惟右軍。

translations.literal: He changed the ancient system; now only the Right General.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the ancient system—now only the Right General.

sentences.zh: 領軍不爾，至今猶法鍾、張。

translations.literal: The Army Commander was not so; to this day one still takes Zhong and Zhang as law.
translations.idiomatic: The Army Commander was not so—to this day one still takes Zhong and Zhang as law.

sentences.zh: 亡從祖中書令書，子敬云：'弟書如騎騾，駸駸恒欲度驊騮前。

translations.literal: The deceased collateral ancestor Palace Secretary's calligraphy—Zijing said, 'Younger brother's calligraphy is like riding a mule, constantly eager to pass the thoroughbred ahead.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: the deceased collateral ancestor Palace Secretary's calligraphy—Zijing said, 'Younger brother's calligraphy is like riding a mule, constantly eager to pass the thoroughbred ahead.

sentences.zh: '庾征西翼書，少時與右軍齊名，右軍後進，庾猶不分。

translations.literal: Western Expeditionary General Yu Yi's calligraphy—in youth matched the Right General's fame; the Right General advanced later, yet Yu still did not concede.
translations.idiomatic: Western Expeditionary General Yu Yi's calligraphy—in youth matched the Right General's fame—the Right General advanced later, yet Yu still did not concede.

sentences.zh: 在荊州與都下人書云：'小兒輩賤家雞，皆學逸少書，須吾下當比之。

translations.literal: In Jing Province he wrote to men of the capital, 'The boy fellows despise the home chicken—all study Yishao's calligraphy; when I come down I shall compare with them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing Province he wrote to men of the capital, 'The boy fellows despise the home chicken—all study Yishao's calligraphy—when I come down I shall compare with them.

sentences.zh: '張翼，王右軍自書表，晉穆帝令翼寫題後答，右軍當時不別，久後方悟，雲'小人幾欲亂真'。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi—the Right General Wang wrote a memorial himself; Emperor Mu of Jin ordered Yi to copy and answer on the back; the Right General at the time did not distinguish it; long afterward he understood and said 'the petty man nearly confused the genuine.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi—the Right General Wang wrote a memorial himself—Emperor Mu of Jin ordered Yi to copy and answer on the back—the Right General at the time did not distinguish it—long afterward he understood and said 'the petty man nearly confused the genuine.'

sentences.zh: 張芝、索靖、韋誕、鍾會、二衛，並得名前代，無以辨其優劣，唯見其筆力驚異耳。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Dan, Zhong Hui, the two Weis—all gained fame in former ages; one cannot distinguish their superiority and inferiority; one only sees their brush strength astonishing and unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Dan, Zhong Hui, the two Weis—all gained fame in former ages—one cannot distinguish their superiority and inferiority—one only sees their brush strength astonishing and unusual.

sentences.zh: 張澄當時亦呼有意。

translations.literal: Zhang Cheng at the time was also called to have intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng then was also called to have intent.

sentences.zh: 郗愔章草亞於右軍。

translations.literal: Xi Yin's draft cursive is next to the Right General.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: xi Yin's draft cursive is next to the Right General.

sentences.zh: 郗嘉賓草亞于二王，緊媚過其父。

translations.literal: Xi Guest's cursive is next to the Two Wangs; tight charm surpasses his father.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Guest's cursive is next to the Two Wangs—tight charm surpasses his father.

sentences.zh: 桓玄自謂右軍之流，論者以比孔琳之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan considered himself of the Right General's stream; commentators compared him to Kong Linzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan considered himself of the Right General's stream—commentators compared him to Kong Linzhi.

sentences.zh: 謝安亦入能書錄，亦自重，為子敬書嵇康詩。

translations.literal: Xie An also entered the record of able calligraphers; he also valued himself and for Zijing wrote Ji Kang's poem.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An also entered the record of able calligraphers—he also valued himself and for Zijing wrote Ji Kang's poem.

sentences.zh: 羊欣書見重一時，親受子敬。

translations.literal: Yang Xin's calligraphy was valued for a time; he personally received Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin's calligraphy was valued for a time—he personally received Zijing.

sentences.zh: 行書尤善，正乃不稱名。

translations.literal: Running script he was especially good at; regular script indeed did not match his name.
translations.idiomatic: Running script he was especially good at—regular script indeed did not match his name.

sentences.zh: 孔琳之書，天然縱放，極有筆力，規矩恐在羊欣後。

translations.literal: Kong Linzhi's calligraphy—natural and unrestrained, extremely powerful in brush; in compass and rule he perhaps comes after Yang Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Linzhi's calligraphy—natural and unrestrained, extremely powerful in brush—in compass and rule he perhaps comes after Yang Xin.

sentences.zh: 丘道護與羊欣俱面受子敬，故當在欣後。

translations.literal: Qiu Daohu and Yang Xin both received Zijing face to face, so he should come after Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Daohu and Yang Xin both received Zijing face to face—so he should come after Xin.

sentences.zh: 范曄與蕭思話同師羊欣，後小叛，既失故步，為復小有意耳。

translations.literal: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua studied under the same master Yang Xin; afterward he rebelled slightly and lost his old step—he again has a little intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua studied under the same master Yang Xin—afterward he rebelled slightly and lost his old step—he again has a little intent.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話書，羊欣之影，風流趨好，殆當不減，筆力恨弱。

translations.literal: Xiao Sihua's calligraphy is Yang Xin's shadow—elegant trend and preference perhaps not less, yet brush strength regrettably weak.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua's calligraphy is Yang Xin's shadow—elegant trend and preference perhaps not less—yet brush strength regrettably weak.

sentences.zh: 謝綜書，其舅雲緊生起。

translations.literal: Xie Zong's calligraphy—his maternal uncle said 'tightness rises from birth.'
translations.idiomatic: Of Xie Zong's calligraphy his maternal uncle remarked that its tightness was inborn.

sentences.zh: 是得賞也，恨少媚好。

translations.literal: This obtains praise, yet regrettably lacks charming grace.
translations.idiomatic: This obtains praise—yet regrettably lacks charming grace.

sentences.zh: 謝靈運書乃不倫，遇其合時，亦得入流。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun's calligraphy is not of the same class; when it meets its moment it also enters the stream.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun's calligraphy is not of the same class—when it meets its moment it also enters the stream.

sentences.zh: 賀道力書亞丘道護。

translations.literal: He Daoli's calligraphy is next to Qiu Daohu.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he Daoli's calligraphy is next to Qiu Daohu.

sentences.zh: 庾昕學右軍，亦欲亂真矣。」

translations.literal: Yu Xin studied the Right General and also wished to confuse the genuine."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin studied the Right General and nearly passed his work off as genuine."

sentences.zh: 僧虔嘗自書讓尚書令表，辭制既雅，筆跡又麗，時人以比子敬崇賢。

translations.literal: Sengqian once himself wrote the memorial declining Director of the Masters of Writing; the diction was elegant and the brush trace beautiful; men of the time compared it to Zijing's Chongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian once himself wrote the memorial declining Director of the Masters of Writing—the diction was elegant and the brush trace beautiful—men of the time compared it to Zijing's Chongxian.

sentences.zh: 吳郡顧寶先卓越多奇，自以伎能，僧虔乃作飛白以示之。

translations.literal: Gu Baoxian of Wu commandery was outstanding with many marvels; trusting his skill, Sengqian made flying-white to show him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Baoxian of Wu commandery was outstanding with many marvels—trusting his skill, Sengqian made flying-white to show him.

sentences.zh: 寶先曰：「下官今為飛白屈矣。

translations.literal: Baoxian said, "This lower official now yields to flying-white.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxian replied, "This lower official now yields to flying-white.

sentences.zh: 」僧虔著書賦，儉為注序甚工。

translations.literal: Sengqian composed a book rhapsody; Jian wrote the preface commentary very skillfully.
translations.idiomatic: Sengqian composed a book rhapsody—Jian wrote the preface commentary very skillfully.

sentences.zh: 僧虔宋世嘗有書誡子曰：

translations.literal: Sengqian in Song times once had a letter admonishing his son:
translations.idiomatic: In Song times Sengqian once wrote his son a letter of admonition:

sentences.zh: 知汝恨吾未許汝學，欲自悔厲，或以闔棺自欺，或更擇美業，且得有慨，亦慰窮生。

translations.literal: Knowing you regret that I did not permit you to study, you wish to repent and spur yourself, or perhaps deceive yourself with closing the coffin, or again choose a fine profession—and to have aspiration is also comfort for a poor life.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing you regret that I did not permit you to study—you wish to repent and spur yourself, or perhaps deceive yourself with closing the coffin, or again choose a fine profession—and to have aspiration is also comfort for a poor life.

sentences.zh: 但亟聞斯唱，未睹其實，吾未信汝，非徒然也。

translations.literal: But I have quickly heard this song and not yet seen the reality—I do not yet believe you; it is not for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: But I have quickly heard this song and not yet seen the reality—I do not yet believe you—it is not for nothing.

sentences.zh: 往年有意于史，取三國志聚置床頭，百日許，復徙業就玄。

translations.literal: In former years you had intent toward history, gathered the Records of the Three Kingdoms and placed them at the bedhead—for a hundred days or so—then shifted profession to Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: In former years you had intent toward history—gathered the Records of the Three Kingdoms and placed them at the bedhead—for a hundred days or so—then shifted profession to Mystery.

sentences.zh: 汝曾未窺其題目，未辨其指歸，而終日自欺人，人不受汝欺也。

translations.literal: You have never peeked at their titles, never distinguished their purport, yet all day deceive people—people do not accept your deception.
translations.idiomatic: You have never peeked at their titles, never distinguished their purport—yet all day deceive people—people do not accept your deception.

sentences.zh: 由吾不學，無以為訓，然重華無嚴父，放勳無令子，亦各由己耳。

translations.literal: Because I do not study there is nothing to take as instruction; yet Chonghua had no stern father, Fangxun had no worthy son—each also follows himself.
translations.idiomatic: Because I do not study there is nothing to take as instruction—yet Chonghua had no stern father, Fangxun had no worthy son—each also follows himself.

sentences.zh: 汝輩竊議，亦當云'阿越不學，何忽自課'？

translations.literal: You fellows whisper in secret—should you not also say 'Elder Yue does not study—why suddenly self-assign'?
translations.idiomatic: You whisper among yourselves—do you not also say, 'Elder Yue never studied; why is he suddenly setting himself lessons'?

sentences.zh: 汝見其一耳，不全爾也。

translations.literal: You see only one side—not entirely so.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: you see only one side—not entirely so.

sentences.zh: 設令吾學如馬、鄭，亦復甚勝，復倍不如，今亦必大減，致之有由，從身上來也。

translations.literal: Suppose my learning were like Ma and Zheng—it would again be very superior; again double inferior—it would now also be greatly reduced; the cause has a source—it comes from the body.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose my learning were like Ma and Zheng—it would again be very superior—again double inferior—it would now also be greatly reduced—the cause has a source—it comes from the body.

sentences.zh: 汝今壯年，自勤數倍，許勝劣及吾耳。

translations.literal: You are now in vigorous years; if you diligently exert yourself several times over, you may win or lose against me.
translations.idiomatic: You are now in vigorous years—if you diligently exert yourself several times over, you may win or lose against me.

sentences.zh: 吾在世雖乏德素，要復推排人間數十許年，故是一舊物，人或以比數汝耳。

translations.literal: I in the world though lacking virtue and plainness, still must push aside men for several tens of years—therefore I am an old thing; people perhaps compare you to the number.
translations.idiomatic: I in the world though lacking virtue and plainness, still must push aside men for several tens of years—therefore I am an old thing—people perhaps compare you to the number.

sentences.zh: 即化之後，若自無調度，誰復知汝事者。

translations.literal: After transformation if you yourself have no discipline, who again will know your affairs?
translations.idiomatic: After transformation if you yourself have no discipline—who again will know your affairs?

sentences.zh: 舍中亦有少負令譽、弱冠越超清級者，于時王家門中，優者龍鳳，劣猶虎豹。

translations.literal: In the household there are also some who bear a little fine reputation and at weak crown leap over clear ranks; in the Wang gate then, the superior are dragon and phoenix, the inferior still tiger and leopard.
translations.idiomatic: In the household there are also some who bear a little fine reputation and at weak crown leap over clear ranks—in the Wang gate then, the superior are dragon and phoenix, the inferior still tiger and leopard.

sentences.zh: 失蔭之後，豈龍虎之議？

translations.literal: After losing shade, how can there be dragon-tiger discussion?
translations.idiomatic: After losing shade—how can there be dragon-tiger discussion?

sentences.zh: 況吾不能為汝蔭，政應各自努力耳。

translations.literal: Moreover I cannot shade you—you should each exert yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: moreover I cannot shade you—you should each exert yourselves.

sentences.zh: 或有身經三公，蔑爾無聞，布衣寒素，卿相屈體，父子貴賤殊，兄弟聲名異，何也？

translations.literal: Some bodies pass through Three Excellencies yet are utterly unknown; plain-clothed cold and plain yet chief ministers bow the body; father and son noble and base differ, brothers' fame and voice differ—why?
translations.idiomatic: Some bodies pass through Three Excellencies yet are utterly unknown—plain-clothed cold and plain yet chief ministers bow the body—father and son noble and base differ, brothers' fame and voice differ—why?

sentences.zh: 體盡讀數百卷書耳。

translations.literal: The body simply reads several hundred scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: the body simply reads several hundred scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 吾今悔無所及，欲以前車誡爾後乘也。

translations.literal: I now regret there is nothing to reach; I wish to use the overturned cart to warn your following carriage.
translations.idiomatic: I now regret there is nothing to reach—I wish to use the overturned cart to warn your following carriage.

sentences.zh: 汝年入立境，方應從宦，兼有室累，何處復得下帷如王郎時邪？

translations.literal: You enter the age of standing; you should from now follow office and also have household burdens—where again can you lower the curtain as in Lord Wang's time?
translations.idiomatic: You enter the age of standing—you should from now follow office and also have household burdens—where again can you lower the curtain as in Lord Wang's time?

sentences.zh: 各在爾身已切，豈復關吾邪！

translations.literal: Each in your own body is already urgent—how again does it concern me!
translations.idiomatic: Each of you already feels the urgency in your own bones—what has that to do with me!

sentences.zh: 鬼唯知愛深松茂柏，寧知子弟毀譽事。

translations.literal: Ghosts only know to love deep pine and lush cypress—how would they know sons and younger brothers' ruin and praise affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: ghosts only know to love deep pine and lush cypress—how would they know sons and younger brothers' ruin and praise affairs.

sentences.zh: 因汝有感，故略敘胸懷。

translations.literal: Because of you I have feeling—therefore I briefly narrate what is in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: because of you I have feeling—therefore I briefly narrate what is in the breast.

sentences.zh: 子慈。

translations.literal: His son Ci.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ci.

sentences.zh: 慈字伯寶。

translations.literal: Ci, styled Bobao.
translations.idiomatic: Ci, courtesy name Bobao.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，外祖宋太宰江夏王義恭迎之內齋，施寶物恣所取，慈取素琴石硯及孝子圖而已，義恭善之。

translations.literal: At eight his maternal grandfather Song Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong welcomed him to the inner study, spread treasures and let him take as he wished; Ci took only plain zither, stone inkstone, and the Filial Son picture—Yigong approved.
translations.idiomatic: At eight his maternal grandfather Song Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong welcomed him to the inner study, spread treasures and let him take as he wished—Ci took only plain zither, stone inkstone, and the Filial Son picture—Yigong approved.

sentences.zh: 袁淑見其幼時，撫其背曰；

translations.literal: Yuan Shu saw him in youth and stroked his back saying;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu saw him as a boy and, stroking his back, said;

sentences.zh: 「叔慈內潤也。」

translations.literal: "Uncle Ci is inwardly moist."
translations.idiomatic: "Young Ci has an inward richness."

sentences.zh: 少與從弟儉共書學。

translations.literal: From youth he with cousin Jian together studied calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood, he with cousin Jian together studied calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 謝鳳子超宗嘗候僧虔，仍往東齋詣慈。

translations.literal: Xie Fengzi Chao once visited Sengqian and then went to the eastern study to visit Ci.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: xie Fengzi Chao once visited Sengqian and then went to the eastern study to visit Ci.

sentences.zh: 慈正學書，未即放筆，超宗曰：「卿書何如虔公？

translations.literal: Ci was just studying calligraphy and did not immediately put down the brush; Chao said, "Your calligraphy—how compared with Lord Qian?
translations.idiomatic: Ci was just studying calligraphy and did not immediately put down the brush; Chao replied, "Your calligraphy—how compared with Lord Qian?

sentences.zh: 」慈曰：「慈書比大人，如雞之比鳳。

translations.literal: Ci said, "Ci's calligraphy compared with the elder is like chicken compared with phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Ci replied, "Ci's calligraphy compared with the elder is like chicken compared with phoenix.

sentences.zh: 」超宗狼狽而退。

translations.literal: Chao withdrew in embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: chao withdrew in embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 十歲時，與蔡興宗子約入寺禮佛，正遇沙門懺，約戲慈曰：「眾僧今日可謂虔虔。

translations.literal: At ten years, with Cai Xingzong's son Yue he entered a temple to worship Buddha and happened upon monks confessing; Yue joked with Ci, "The multitude of monks today may be called devout.
translations.idiomatic: At ten years, with Cai Xingzong's son Yue he entered a temple to worship Buddha and happened upon monks confessing—Yue joked with Ci, "The multitude of monks today may be called devout.

sentences.zh: 」慈應聲曰：「卿如此，何以興蔡氏之宗。

translations.literal: Ci answered on the spot, "You like this—how will you raise the Cai clan's lineage?
translations.idiomatic: Ci answered on the spot—"You like this—how will you raise the Cai clan's lineage?

sentences.zh: 」歷位吳郡太守，大司馬長史，侍中，領步兵校尉，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He served successively as Governor of Wu commandery, Chief Secretary to the Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant, Commandant of the Footsoldiers, Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He held a succession of posts: Governor of Wu commandery, Chief Secretary to the Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant, Commandant of the Footsoldiers, Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 慈患腳，齊武帝敕王晏：「慈有微疾，不能騎，聽乘車在仗後。

translations.literal: Ci suffered from the foot; Emperor Wu of Qi ordered Wang Yan, "Ci has a slight ailment and cannot ride—permit him to ride in a carriage behind the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ci suffered from the foot—Emperor Wu of Qi ordered Wang Yan, "Ci has a slight ailment and cannot ride—permit him to ride in a carriage behind the guard.

sentences.zh: 」江左以來少例也。

translations.literal: Since the Eastern Jin there have been few precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: since the Eastern Jin there have been few precedents.

sentences.zh: 慈妻劉彥節女，子觀尚武帝長女吳縣公主，修婦禮，姑未嘗交答。

translations.idiomatic: Ci's wife was Liu Yanjie's daughter—his son Guan married Emperor Wu's eldest daughter Princess of Wu county and observed daughter-in-law ritual—the mother-in-law never exchanged replies.

sentences.zh: 江夏王鋒為南徐州，王妃，慈女也，以慈為東海太守，行南徐州府州事。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Feng was Southern Xuzhou; the princess consort was Ci's daughter; Ci was made Governor of Donghai, acting Southern Xuzhou prefectural and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangxia Feng was Southern Xuzhou—the princess consort was Ci's daughter—Ci was made Governor of Donghai, acting Southern Xuzhou prefectural and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 還為冠軍將軍、廬陵王中軍長史，未拜，永明九年卒。

translations.literal: He returned as General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Chief Secretary to Prince of Luling's Central Army; before accepting, in the ninth year of Yongming he died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Chief Secretary to Prince of Luling's Central Army; before accepting, in Yongming 9 he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太常，諡懿。

sentences.zh: 子泰。

translations.literal: His son Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰字仲通，幼敏悟。

translations.literal: Tai, styled Zhongtong, from youth clever and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Tai, courtesy name Zhongtong, from youth clever and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 年數歲時，祖母集諸孫侄，散棗栗於床，群兒競之，泰獨不取。

translations.literal: At several years his grandmother gathered the various grandsons and nephews, scattered jujubes and chestnuts on the bed; the group of boys competed for them—Tai alone did not take.
translations.idiomatic: At several years his grandmother gathered the various grandsons and nephews, scattered jujubes and chestnuts on the bed—the group of boys competed for them—Tai alone did not take.

sentences.zh: 問其故，對曰：「不取自當得賜。

translations.idiomatic: Asked the reason—he replied, "Not taking—one should naturally receive bestowal.

sentences.zh: 」由是中表異之。

translations.literal: On this account kin by marriage regarded him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: on this account kin by marriage regarded him as unusual.

sentences.zh: 少好學，手所抄寫二千許卷。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; what his hand copied was about two thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood, he loved learning; what his hand copied was about two thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 及長，通和溫雅，家人不見喜慍之色。

translations.literal: When grown he was harmonious and warm and elegant; the household never saw anger or pleasure on his face.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was harmonious and warm and elegant—the household never saw anger or pleasure on his face.

sentences.zh: 姊夫齊江夏王鋒為齊明帝害，外生蕭子友並孤弱，泰資給撫訓，逾于子侄。

translations.literal: Brother-in-law Prince of Jiangxia Feng of Qi was killed by Emperor Ming of Qi; maternal nephew Xiao Ziyou was also orphaned and weak—Tai supplied and nurtured them beyond sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Brother-in-law Prince of Jiangxia Feng of Qi was killed by Emperor Ming of Qi—maternal nephew Xiao Ziyou was also orphaned and weak—Tai supplied and nurtured them beyond sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 始革大理，以泰為廷尉卿，再曆侍中，後為都官尚書。

translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of reforming the Grand Court of Justice, Tai was made Minister of the Court of Justice—he served twice as Palace Attendant, later Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 泰能接人士，故每願其居選官。

translations.literal: Tai could receive men of the realm; therefore each time they wished him to hold the selection office.
translations.idiomatic: Tai could receive men of the realm—therefore each time they wished him to hold the selection office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為吏部尚書，衣冠屬望。

translations.literal: Before long he was Minister of the Masters of Writing; the gentry looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was Minister of the Masters of Writing—the gentry looked to him.

sentences.zh: 未及選舉，仍疾，改除散騎常侍、左驍騎將軍，未拜，卒，諡夷。

translations.literal: Before he could conduct selection he fell ill; he was changed to Cavalier Attendant Regular and General of the Left Valiant Cavalry; before accepting he died; his posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could conduct selection he fell ill—he was changed to Cavalier Attendant Regular and General of the Left Valiant Cavalry—before accepting he died—his posthumous title was Yi.

sentences.zh: 子廓。

translations.literal: His son Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kuo.

sentences.zh: 志字次道，慈之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Cidao, was Ci's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Cidao, was Ci's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 九歲，居所生母憂，哀容毀瘠，為中表所異。

translations.literal: At nine he entered mourning for his birth mother; grieving countenance wasted and emaciated—kin by marriage regarded him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he entered mourning for his birth mother—grieving countenance wasted and emaciated—kin by marriage regarded him as unusual.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，選尚宋孝武女安固公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: At weak crown he was chosen to marry Emperor Xiaowu of Song's daughter Princess of Angu and was made Commandant of the Horse Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At weak crown he would later be chosen to marry Emperor Xiaowu of Song's daughter Princess of Angu and was made Commandant of the Horse Guard.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回為司徒，引志為主簿。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui was Minister of Education and appointed Zhi chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui would later be Minister of Education and appointed Zhi chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 謂其父僧虔曰：「朝廷之恩，本為殊特，所可光榮，在屈賢子。」

translations.literal: He told his father Sengqian, "The court's grace was originally for special distinction; what can bring glory is bending to the worthy son.
translations.idiomatic: He told his father Sengqian, "The court's grace was originally for special distinction—what can bring glory is bending to the worthy son.

sentences.zh: 累遷宣城內史，清謹有恩惠。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to Interior Minister of Xuancheng, pure and careful with kindness and grace.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive appointments he rose to Interior Minister of Xuancheng, pure and careful with kindness and grace.

sentences.zh: 郡人張倪、吳慶爭田，經年不決。

translations.literal: District men Zhang Ni and Wu Qing disputed fields; for years no decision.
translations.idiomatic: District men Zhang Ni and Wu Qing disputed fields—for years no decision.

sentences.zh: 志到官，父老相謂曰：「王府君有德政，吾鄉里乃有如此爭。

translations.literal: When Zhi arrived, the elders said to one another, "Lord Wang has virtuous governance—yet in our district there is such dispute.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi arrived, the elders told one another, "Lord Wang has virtuous governance—yet in our district there is such dispute.

sentences.zh: 」倪、慶因相攜請罪，所訟地遂成閒田。

translations.literal: Ni and Qing thereupon together came bearing guilt; the litigated land became idle fields.
translations.idiomatic: Ni and Qing thereupon together came bearing guilt—the litigated land became idle fields.

sentences.zh: 後為東陽太守，郡獄有重囚十餘，冬至日，悉遣還家，過節皆反，唯一人失期。

translations.literal: Later he was Governor of Dongyang; in the commandery prison were more than ten heavy prisoners; on the winter solstice day he sent them all home; passing the festival all returned—only one man missed the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Governor of Dongyang; in the commandery prison were more than ten heavy prisoners; on the winter solstice day he sent them all home; passing the festival all returned—only one man missed the deadline.

sentences.zh: 志曰：「此自太守事，主者勿憂。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "This is naturally the governor's affair—the responsible officer need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied, "This is naturally the governor's affair—the responsible officer need not worry.

sentences.zh: 」明旦果至，以婦孕。

translations.literal: Next dawn he indeed came—because his wife was pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: Next dawn he indeed came—because his wife would later be pregnant.

sentences.zh: 吏人益嘆服之。

translations.literal: Officials and people further sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 為吏部尚書，在選以和理稱。

translations.literal: He was Minister of the Masters of Writing; in selection he was praised for harmony and reason.
translations.idiomatic: He was Minister of the Masters of Writing—in selection he was praised for harmony and reason.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景平，以例加右軍將軍，封臨汝侯。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing was pacified, by precedent Right Army General was added and he was enfeoffed Marquis of Linru.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing was pacified—by precedent Right Army General was added and he was enfeoffed Marquis of Linru.

sentences.zh: 固讓，改領右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and was changed to hold Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He declined firmly and was reassigned as hold Right Guard General instead.

sentences.zh: 及梁武軍至，城內殺東昏，百僚署名送首。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang's army arrived, within the city Emperor Donghun was killed; the hundred officials signed names and sent the head.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang's army arrived, within the city Emperor Donghun was killed—the hundred officials signed names and sent the head.

sentences.zh: 志歎曰：「冠雖弊，可加足乎？

translations.literal: Zhi sighed and said, "Though the cap is worn out, can the foot be added?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sighed and replied, "Though the cap is worn out, can the foot be added?

sentences.zh: 」因取庭樹葉捼服之，偽悶不署名。

translations.literal: He thereupon took courtyard tree leaves, rubbed them on his garment, feigned distress and did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon took courtyard tree leaves—rubbed them on his garment, feigned distress and did not sign.

sentences.zh: 梁武覽箋無志署，心嘉之，弗以讓也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu reading the memorial saw no Zhi signature; he admired this in his heart and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu reading the memorial saw no Zhi signature—he admired this in his heart and did not blame him.

sentences.zh: 霸府開，為驃騎大將軍長史，梁台建，位散騎常侍、中書令。

translations.literal: When the regency office opened he was Chief Secretary to the General of Agile Cavalry; when the Liang regime was established he was Cavalier Attendant Regular and Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the regency office opened he was Chief Secretary to the General of Agile Cavalry—when the Liang regime was established he was Cavalier Attendant Regular and Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 天監初，為丹陽尹，為政清靜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Governor of Danyang; his governance was pure and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian he was Governor of Danyang—his governance was pure and quiet.

sentences.zh: 部下有寡婦無子，姑亡舉責以斂，葬既而無以還之。

translations.literal: Under his jurisdiction was a widow without a son; when the mother-in-law died she borrowed to pay for burial; after burial there was no means to repay.
translations.idiomatic: Under his jurisdiction was a widow without a son—when the mother-in-law died she borrowed to pay for burial—after burial there was no means to repay.

sentences.zh: 志湣其義，以俸錢償焉。

translations.literal: Zhi pitied her righteousness and repaid with salary money.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: zhi pitied her righteousness and repaid with salary money.

sentences.zh: 時年饑，每旦為粥於郡門以賦百姓，眾悉稱惠。

translations.literal: At the time there was famine; each dawn he made gruel at the commandery gate to give the hundred families—all praised his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, there was famine; each dawn he made gruel at the commandery gate to give the hundred families—all praised his kindness.

sentences.zh: 常懷止足，謂諸子侄曰：「謝莊在宋孝武時，位止中書令，吾自視豈可過之。

translations.literal: He constantly held stopping and sufficiency and told sons and nephews, "Xie Zhuang in Emperor Xiaowu of Song's time stopped at Palace Secretary—I compare myself: how can I surpass that?
translations.idiomatic: He always kept to knowing when to stop and told sons and nephews, "In Emperor Xiaowu of Song's day Xie Zhuang rose no higher than Palace Secretary—when I measure myself against that, how could I go further?

sentences.zh: 」三年，為散騎常侍、中書令，因多謝病，簡通賓客。

translations.literal: In the third year he was Cavalier Attendant Regular and Palace Secretary; thereupon he often declined illness and simplified receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was Cavalier Attendant Regular and Palace Secretary—thereupon he often declined illness and simplified receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 九年，還為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he returned as Cavalier Attendant Regular and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and died.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: in the ninth year he returned as Cavalier Attendant Regular and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and died.

sentences.zh: 志善草隸，當時以為楷法。

translations.literal: Zhi excelled at cursive and clerical script; the age at the time took it as model law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi excelled at cursive and clerical script—the age at the time took it as model law.

sentences.zh: 齊遊擊將軍徐希秀亦號能書，常謂志為「書聖」。

translations.literal: Qi Raiding General Xu Xixiu also was called able at calligraphy; he often called Zhi "Sage of Calligraphy."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Raiding General Xu Xixiu also was called able at calligraphy—he often called Zhi "Sage of Calligraphy."

translations.literal: Zhi's house dwelt in Mafen Lane inside the Jianye forbidden quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: zhi's house dwelt in Mafen Lane inside the Jianye forbidden quarter.

translations.literal: His father Sengqian's gate wind was broad and forgiving; Zhi was especially sincere and thick; what he passed through he never used guilt and blame to impeach people.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengqian's gate wind was broad and forgiving—Zhi was especially sincere and thick—what he passed through he never used guilt and blame to impeach people.

sentences.zh: 門下客嘗盜脫志車幰賣之，志知而不問，待之如初。

translations.literal: A guest once stole and removed Zhi's carriage canopy to sell; Zhi knew yet did not inquire and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: A guest once stole and removed Zhi's carriage canopy to sell—Zhi knew yet did not inquire and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 賓客遊其門者，專蓋其過而稱其善。

translations.literal: Guests who passed his gate exclusively covered their faults and praised their goodness.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: guests who passed his gate exclusively covered their faults and praised their goodness.

sentences.zh: 兄弟子侄皆篤實謙和，時人號馬糞諸王為長者。

translations.literal: Brothers' sons and nephews were all solid and modest and harmonious; men of the time called the Wangs of Mafen Lane elders.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers' sons and nephews were all solid and modest and harmonious—men of the time called the Wangs of Mafen Lane elders.

sentences.zh: 普通四年，志改葬，武帝厚賻贈之，諡曰安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Putong Zhi changed burial; Emperor Wu richly sent funeral gifts; his posthumous title was An.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 4 Zhi changed burial; Emperor Wu richly sent funeral gifts; his posthumous title was An.

sentences.zh: 有五子：緝、休、諲、操、素。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Ji, Xiu, Yin, Cao, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Ji, Xiu, Yin, Cao—and Su.

sentences.zh: 志弟揖位太中大夫，揖子筠。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Yi held Grand Master of the Palace; Yi's son Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Yi held Grand Master of the Palace—Yi's son Yun.

sentences.zh: 筠字元禮，一字德柔，幼而警悟，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Yun, styled Yuanli, one character Derou; from youth clever and penetrating; at seven could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, courtesy name Yuanli, also styled Derou; from youth clever and penetrating; at seven could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 年十六，為芍藥賦，其辭甚美。

translations.literal: At sixteen he composed a Peony rhapsody; the wording was very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he composed a Peony rhapsody—the wording was very beautiful.

sentences.zh: 及長，清靜好學，與從兄泰齊名。

translations.literal: When grown he was pure and quiet and loved learning; with cousin Tai he was equally famed.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was pure and quiet and loved learning—with cousin Tai he was equally famed.

translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "Lord Yuan seeing people always stern and strict; Lord Wang seeing people always entertains with laughter.

sentences.zh: 唯此一條，不能酷似。」

translations.literal: Only in this one point he cannot closely resemble."

translations.literal: He served as Director in the Masters of Writing Hall; since the Wang clan crossed the river there had never been one in the directorate; some urged him not to accept—Yun said, "Lu Pingyuan was the southeast's fine talent; Wang Wendu alone walked the Jiang east.

translations.literal: That I can compare tracks with men of old—what is there much to regret?
translations.idiomatic: To walk in the footsteps of men of old—what more could I regret?

translations.literal: He thereupon gladly took office.
translations.idiomatic: He then gladly took office.

translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shen Yue read Yun's writing he sighed with admiration and once told him, "Long ago, when Cai Bojie met Wang Zhongxuan, he said, 'Lord Wang's grandson deserves every book in my house.'

translations.literal: Your servant though not clever asks to attach to this saying.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: your servant though not clever asks to attach to this saying.

sentences.zh: 自謝朓諸賢零落，平生意好殆絕，不謂疲暮復逢於君。

translations.literal: Since Xie Tiao and the various worthies fell away, the life's intent and pleasure is nearly gone—unexpected in weary evening again to meet you.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xie Tiao and the various worthies fell away—the life's intent and pleasure is nearly gone—unexpected in weary evening again to meet you.

translations.idiomatic: In sum: yue at his suburban residence pavilion study asked Yun for ten plant poems to write on the wall—all directly writing the text without adding section titles.

translations.idiomatic: Yue told people—"These poems point at things and measure form—no need to borrow titles.

sentences.zh: 」約制郊居賦，構思積時，猶未都畢，示筠草。

translations.literal: Yue composed the Suburban Residence rhapsody, structuring thought for long time yet not all complete; he showed Yun the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Yue composed the Suburban Residence rhapsody, structuring thought for long time yet not all complete—he showed Yun the draft.

sentences.zh: 筠讀至「雌霓」。

translations.literal: Yun read to 'female rainbow.'
translations.idiomatic: Yun read as far as the line on the secondary rainbow.

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to Heir Apparent Purifier, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, both managing Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive appointments he rose to Heir Apparent Purifier, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, both managing Eastern Palace records.

translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming loved literary scholars; he often with Yun and Liu Xiaochuo, Lu Chui, Dao Qia, Yin Jun and others feasted and wandered in the Mystic Garden; the crown prince alone grasped Yun's sleeve, stroked Xiaochuo's shoulder and replied, "What is called left holding Floating Hill's sleeve, right patting Hongya's shoulder.
