translations.literal: Such was the weight he received.
translations.idiomatic: Such would later be the weight he received.

sentences.zh: 筠又與殷鈞以方雅見禮。

translations.literal: Yun also with Yin Jun was honored with square elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Yun also with Yin Jun would later be honored with square elegance.

sentences.zh: 後為中書郎，奉敕制開善寺寶志法師碑文，辭甚麗逸。

translations.literal: Later he was Palace Secretary; by imperial order he composed the stele text for Master Baozhi of Kaishan Temple—the diction very beautiful and flowing.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Palace Secretary; by imperial order he composed the stele text for Master Baozhi of Kaishan Temple—the diction very beautiful and flowing.

sentences.zh: 又敕撰中書表奏三十卷，及所上賦頌都為一集。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to compile thirty scrolls of palace memorials and petitions, and the submitted rhapsodies and eulogies were all made one collection.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to compile thirty scrolls of palace memorials and petitions—and the submitted rhapsodies and eulogies were all made one collection.

sentences.zh: 後為太子家令，復掌管記。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief of the Heir Apparent's Household, again managing records.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Chief of the Heir Apparent's Household, again managing records.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he left office on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong 1 he left office on his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 筠有孝性，毀瘠過禮。

translations.literal: Yun had filial nature; wasting and emaciation exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had filial nature—wasting and emaciation exceeded ritual.

sentences.zh: 中大通二年，為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongdatong he was Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong 2 he was Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 三年，昭明太子薨，敕制哀策文，復見嗟賞。

translations.literal: In the third year Crown Prince Zhaoming died; he was ordered to compose the lamentation text and again received sighing praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Crown Prince Zhaoming died—he was ordered to compose the lamentation text and again received sighing praise.

sentences.zh: 尋出為臨海太守，在郡侵刻，還資有芒屩兩舫，他物稱是。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Linhai; in the commandery he was harsh and grasping; returned goods had two boatloads of straw sandals—other goods matched this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as Governor of Linhai—in the commandery he was harsh and grasping—returned goods had two boatloads of straw sandals—other goods matched this.

sentences.zh: 為有司奏，不調累年。

translations.literal: He was memorialized by the responsible officials; for years he was not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He was memorialized by the responsible officials—for years he was not transferred.

sentences.zh: 後曆秘書監，太府卿，度支尚書，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Director of the Secretariat, Minister of the Treasury, Minister of Revenue, Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Director of the Secretariat—Minister of the Treasury, Minister of Revenue, Senior Secretary of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 及簡文即位，為太子詹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen acceded he was Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen acceded he would later be Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 筠家累千金，性儉嗇，外服粗弊，所乘牛嘗飼以青草。

translations.literal: The Yun household accumulated a thousand gold; by nature he was frugal and stingy; outer dress coarse and worn; the ox he rode was often fed green grass.
translations.idiomatic: The Yun household accumulated a thousand gold—by nature he was frugal and stingy—outer dress coarse and worn—the ox he rode was often fed green grass.

sentences.zh: 及遇亂，舊宅先為賊焚，乃寓居國子祭酒蕭子雲宅。

translations.literal: When disorder came the old residence was first burned by bandits; he then lodged at National University Director Xiao Ziyun's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When disorder came the old residence was first burned by bandits—he then lodged at National University Director Xiao Ziyun's residence.

sentences.zh: 夜忽有盜攻，懼墜井，卒，時年六十九。

translations.literal: At night suddenly bandits attacked; fearing falling into a well he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At night suddenly bandits attacked—fearing falling into a well he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 家人十三口同遇害，人棄屍積于空井中。

translations.literal: Thirteen household members met harm together; people cast corpses piled in the empty well.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen household members met harm together—people cast corpses piled in the empty well.

sentences.zh: 筠狀貌寢小，長不滿六尺。

translations.literal: Yun's form and appearance were small and short; height did not fill six chi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's form and appearance were small and short—height did not fill six chi.

sentences.zh: 性弘厚，不以藝能高人。

translations.literal: By nature he was broad and thick and did not set himself above others by skill.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament he was broad and generous and did not set himself above others by skill.

sentences.zh: 而少擅才名，與劉孝綽見重當時。

translations.literal: Yet from youth he monopolized talent and name; with Liu Xiaochuo he was valued in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from youth he monopolized talent and name—with Liu Xiaochuo he was valued in the age.

sentences.zh: 其自序云：「餘少好抄書，老而彌篤，雖偶見瞥觀，皆即疏記。

translations.literal: His self-preface says, "From youth I loved copying books; old I grow more earnest; though occasionally seeing a glance I immediately note it.
translations.idiomatic: His self-preface says, "From youth I loved copying books—old I grow more earnest—though occasionally seeing a glance I immediately note it.

sentences.zh: 後重省覽，歡興彌深。

translations.literal: Later reviewing again, joy and interest grow deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Later reviewing again—joy and interest grow deeper.

sentences.zh: 習與性成，不覺筆倦。

translations.literal: Practice and nature become one—I do not feel brush weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: practice and nature become one—I do not feel brush weariness.

sentences.zh: 自年十三四，建武二年乙亥，至梁大同六年，四十六載矣。

translations.literal: From age thirteen or fourteen, yihai of the second year of Jianwu, to the sixth year of Datong of Liang—forty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: From age thirteen or fourteen, yihai of Jianwu 2, to Datong 6 of Liang—forty-six years.

sentences.zh: 幼年讀五經，皆七八十遍。

translations.literal: In youth I read the Five Classics—all seven or eight tens of times.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: in youth I read the Five Classics—all seven or eight tens of times.

sentences.zh: 愛左氏春秋，吟諷常為口實。

translations.literal: I loved the Zuo Commentary to Spring and Autumn; chanting and reciting often became words in the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: I loved the Zuo Commentary to Spring and Autumn—chanting and reciting often became words in the mouth.

sentences.zh: 廣略去取，凡三過五抄，余經及周官、儀禮、國語、爾雅、山海經、本草並再抄，子史諸集皆一遍。

translations.literal: Broadly skimming and selecting—altogether three passes five copies; remaining classics and Offices of Zhou, Ceremonies, Rites, Discourses, Erya, Classic of Mountains and Seas, Materia Medica—all again copied; histories and various collections all once.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly skimming and selecting—altogether three passes five copies—remaining classics and Offices of Zhou, Ceremonies, Rites, Discourses, Erya, Classic of Mountains and Seas, Materia Medica—all again copied—histories and various collections all once.

sentences.zh: 未嘗倩人假手，並躬自抄錄，大小百餘卷。

translations.literal: Never borrowed another's hand—all personally copied; large and small more than a hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Never borrowed another's hand—all personally copied—large and small more than a hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 不足傳之好事，蓋以備遺忘而已。

translations.literal: Not enough to transmit to those who love such things—simply to prepare against forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: not enough to transmit to those who love such things—simply to prepare against forgetting.

sentences.zh: 」又與諸兒書論家門集云：「史傳稱安平崔氏及汝南應氏並累葉有文才，所以范蔚宗雲崔氏雕龍。

translations.literal: He also in a letter to the various sons discussed the gate clan collection: "Historical records call the Anping Cui clan and Runan Ying clan both successive generations with literary talent—therefore Fan Ye said the Cui clan carved dragons.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he also in a letter to the various sons discussed the gate clan collection: "Historical records call the Anping Cui clan and Runan Ying clan both successive generations with literary talent—therefore Fan Ye said the Cui clan carved dragons.

sentences.zh: 然不過父子兩三世耳，非有七葉之中，名德重光，爵位相繼，人人有集，如吾門者也。

translations.literal: Yet it was only father and son two three generations—not seven generations within, fame and virtue heavy and bright, rank and position successive, every man with a collection, like our gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it would later be only father and son two three generations—not seven generations within, fame and virtue heavy and bright, rank and position successive, every man with a collection, like our gate.

sentences.zh: 沈少傅約常語人云∶'吾少好百家之言，身為四代之史。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Shen often told people: 'From youth I loved the hundred schools' words; body is historian of four dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Shen often told people: 'From youth I loved the hundred schools' words—body is historian of four dynasties.

sentences.zh: 自開闢以來，未有爵位蟬聯、文才相繼如王氏之盛也。

translations.literal: From opening to the present, never has rank and position continued like cicada shell, literary talent successive like the Wang clan's flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: From opening to the present—never has rank and position continued like cicada shell, literary talent successive like the Wang clan's flourishing.

sentences.zh: '汝等仰觀堂構，思各努力。

translations.literal: You fellows look up at the hall structure—think each to exert yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: you fellows look up at the hall structure—think each to exert yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」筠自撰其文章，以一官為一集，自洗馬、中書、中庶、吏部、左佐、臨海、太府各十卷，尚書三十卷，凡一百卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Yun himself compiled his literary compositions—one office one collection; from Purifier, Palace Secretary, Junior Mentor, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Left Aide, Linhai, Grand Treasury each ten scrolls, Masters of Writing thirty scrolls—altogether one hundred scrolls, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yun himself compiled his literary compositions—one office one collection—from Purifier, Palace Secretary, Junior Mentor, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Left Aide, Linhai, Grand Treasury each ten scrolls, Masters of Writing thirty scrolls—altogether one hundred scrolls, circulating in the world.

sentences.zh: 子祥，仕陳位黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Xiang served Chen as Palace Secretary and Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: his son Xiang served Chen as Palace Secretary and Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 揖弟彬。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Bin.

sentences.zh: 彬字思文，好文章，習篆隸，與志齊名。

translations.literal: Bin, styled Siwen, loved literary composition, practiced seal and clerical script; with Zhi he was equally famed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, courtesy name Siwen, loved literary composition, practiced seal and clerical script; with Zhi he was equally famed.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「三真六草，為天下寶。

translations.literal: Men of the time made a saying of it: "Three regular and six cursive—treasure of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: men of the time made a saying of it: "Three regular and six cursive—treasure of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」齊武帝起舊宮，彬獻賦，文辭典麗。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi raised the old palace; Bin presented a rhapsody; the wording classic and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi raised the old palace—Bin presented a rhapsody—the wording classic and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 尚齊高帝女臨海長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Gao of Qi's daughter Princess Chang of Linhai and was made Commandant of the Horse Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Gao of Qi's daughter Princess Chang of Linhai and would later be made Commandant of the Horse Guard.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，曆太子中庶子，徙永嘉太守。

translations.literal: He served Qi, successively Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; he was transferred Governor of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: He served Qi, successively Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent—he was transferred Governor of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 卜室于積穀山，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: He chose a dwelling on Jigu Mountain with intent to end there.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he chose a dwelling on Jigu Mountain with intent to end there.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，曆吏部尚書、秘書監。

translations.literal: In Liang Tianjian he successively served Minister of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang Tianjian he in turn served Minister of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡惠。

translations.literal: When he died his posthumous title was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his posthumous title was Hui.

sentences.zh: 彬立身清白，推賢接士，有士君子風。

translations.literal: Bin established himself pure and white, promoted the worthy and received scholars—he had the wind of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Bin established himself pure and white—promoted the worthy and received scholars—he had the wind of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 彬弟寂。

translations.literal: Bin's younger brother Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's younger brother Ji.

sentences.zh: 寂字子玄，性迅動，好文章。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Zixuan, by nature quick and active, loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, courtesy name Zixuan, by nature quick and active, loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 讀范滂傳，未嘗不歎悒。

translations.literal: Reading Fan Pang's biography he never failed to sigh in distress.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: reading Fan Pang's biography he never failed to sigh in distress.

sentences.zh: 王融敗後，賓客多歸之。

translations.literal: After Wang Rong's fall guests mostly returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: after Wang Rong's fall guests mostly returned to him.

sentences.zh: 齊建武初，欲獻中興頌，兄志謂曰：「汝膏粱年少，何患不達？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu of Qi he wished to present a Zhongxing eulogy; elder brother Zhi told him, "You are rich young meat—what fear of not reaching?
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianwu of Qi he wished to present a Zhongxing eulogy—elder brother Zhi told him, "You are rich young meat—what fear of not reaching?

sentences.zh: 不鎮之以靜，將恐貽譏。

translations.literal: If you do not stabilize with stillness, I fear you will invite ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not stabilize with stillness—I fear you will invite ridicule.

sentences.zh: 」寂乃止。

translations.literal: Ji thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ji thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 位秘書郎。

translations.literal: He held Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he held Secretary.

sentences.zh: 卒年二十一。

translations.literal: He died aged twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In sum: he died aged twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王曇首之才器，王僧綽之忠直，其世祿不替也，豈徒然哉。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Wang Tanshou's talent and capacity, Wang Sengchuo's loyalty and uprightness—their hereditary stipend undiminished—is it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: The judgment says: Wang Tanshou's talent and capacity—Wang Sengchuo's loyalty and uprightness—their hereditary stipend undiminished—is it for nothing?

sentences.zh: 仲寶雅道自居，早懷伊、呂之志，竟而逢時遇主，自致宰輔之隆，所謂衣冠禮樂盡在是矣。

translations.literal: Zhongbao took elegant conduct as his dwelling, early harbored the ambition of Yi and Lü; in the end he met the time and encountered his lord, himself reaching chief minister's eminence—what is called caps and robes, rites and music all were in this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongbao took elegant conduct as his dwelling, early harbored the ambition of Yi and Lü—in the end he met the time and encountered his lord, himself reaching chief minister's eminence—what is called caps and robes, rites and music all were in this.

sentences.zh: 齊有人焉，于斯為盛。

translations.literal: In Qi there were such men—here was the flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi there were such men—here would later be the flourishing.

sentences.zh: 其餘文雅儒素，各稟家風，箕裘不墜，亦云美矣。

translations.literal: The rest, refined and Confucian plain, each received the gate wind; robe and fur did not fall—also called beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The rest, refined and Confucian plain, each received the gate wind—robe and fur did not fall—also called beautiful.
